en: A decision on an issue of fact in a civil or criminal case or an inquest.
An opinion or judgement.

verdict.ety: From Middle English verdit, from Anglo-Norman verdit (> Medieval Latin veredictum), from veir (“true”) + dit (“saying”); possibly a calque of a Germanic term such as Old English sōþword, sōþsprǣċ, sōþspell, sōþsagu, or sōþcwide, all meaning "true story, statement of truth, account, history". Doublet of veredictum.

ex.en: The jury has returned a verdict of guilty.
ex.ja: 陪審員は有罪の判決を答申した。

ex.en: The verdict is a tribute to their fairness.
ex.ja: 評決は公平な審議の証拠である。

ex.en: The jury's guilty verdict gave rise to widespread debate.
ex.ja: 陪審団による有罪評決が大論争の引き金となった。

note.ja: ver（真実）+ dict（言う）。真実を言うこと →「（陪審の）評決・判断」。

To cause to come to agreement; to bring about harmony; to reconcile.

ex.en: I accommodated my plan to those new circumstances.
ex.ja: 私は自分の計画をその新しい状況に適合させた。

en: Agreeably; correspondingly; suitably.
In natural sequence; consequently; so.

accordingly.ety: From Middle English acordingli, equivalent to according + -ly.

ex.en: She was asked to go, and she left accordingly.
ex.ja: 彼女は行くように頼まれた、だから出かけた。

ex.en: Watch your leader and act accordingly.
ex.ja: よくリーダーを見て、その通りに動きなさい。

ex.en: Accordingly I gave up my plans.
ex.ja: そこで私は自分の計画を断念した。

note.ja: accord（一致する）+ -ingly。accord は ad（〜に）+ cor（心）。「心を合わせて」→「それに応じて」。

The study of art or beauty.
That which appeals to the senses.

ex.ja: トムには近代絵画の鑑賞能力がある。

ex.en: What is it that satisfies your aesthetic sense?
ex.ja: あなたの美意識を満足させるものは何ですか？

ex.en: Their furniture is more aesthetic than practical.
ex.ja: 彼らの家具は実用的と言うよりも美的である。

en: A collection of ordered steps that solve a mathematical problem. A precise step-by-step plan for a computational procedure that possibly …
A flow chart illustrating a decision-making process for human users, especially health care professionals.

en: A tool used to moor a vessel to the bottom of a sea or river to resist movement.
An iron device so shaped as to grip the bottom and hold a vessel at her berth by the chain or rope attached.
To connect an object, especially a ship or a boat, to a fixed point.
To cast anchor; to come to anchor.

From Middle English anker, from Old English ancor, ancra, from Latin ancora, from (or cognate with) Ancient Greek ἄγκυρα (ánkura). The modern form is a sixteenth-century modification after the Medieval Latin spelling anchora. Doublet of ancora, anker, angora, and Ankara.

ex.en: His mother's letters were an anchor to the boy.
ex.ja: 少年にとって母の手紙は心の支えだった。

ex.en: A big ship is anchored near here.
ex.ja: 大きな船が、湾内にいかりをおろしている。

ex.en: The ship is at anchor in the harbor.
ex.ja: その船は港に停泊している。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 ankyra（錨）から。「曲がったもの」が原義。「船をつなぎ止める物」→ 番組をつなぎ止める人 →「ニュースキャスター」。angle（角）と同系とされる。

en: An inverted U shape.
An arch-shaped arrangement of trapezoidal stones, designed to redistribute downward force outward.
To form into an arch shape.
To cover with an arch or arches.
Knowing, clever, mischievous.
Cute, sly, prematurely wise.

From Middle English arch, arche, from Old French arche (“an arch”), a feminine form of arc, from Latin arcus (“a bow, arc, arch”). Doublet of arc and arco. Displaced native Old English bīeġels and Old English hwealf.

ex.en: Cats arch their backs.
ex.ja: 猫は背中を丸める。

note.ja: ラテン語 arcus（弓）から。「アーチ・弓なりにする」。arc、arrow と同系。「主要な」の arch-（archenemy）は別語。

en: An imaginary line around which an object spins (an axis of rotation) or is symmetrically arranged (an axis of symmetry).
A fixed one-dimensional figure, such as a line or arc, with an origin and orientation and such that its points are in one-to-one correspo…

Borrowed from Latin axis (“axle, axis”) in the 16th century. Via Latin cognate with ala, aisle, atelier. Via Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱs- cognate with inherited English axle and borrowed axo-, axon.

ex.en: He played an important part like an axis.
ex.ja: 彼は軸のような重要な役割を演じた。

ex.en: It's common knowledge that the earth turns on its axis.
ex.ja: 地球が自転しているのは常識だ。

ex.en: The hand on its axis turns at 10 revolutions per hour.
ex.ja: 針は中心を一時間に１０回転の割合で回る。

note.ja: ラテン語 axis（車軸）から。axle（車軸）と同系。「回転の中心」→「軸」。

en: A distinctive mark, token, sign, emblem or cognizance, worn on one’s clothing, as an insignia of some rank, or of the membership of an or…
A small nameplate, identifying the wearer, and often giving additional information.
To mark or distinguish with a badge.
To show a badge to.

badge.ety: From Middle English badge, bagge, bage, bagy, from Anglo-Norman bage or Medieval Latin bagea, bagia (“sign, emblem”), of uncertain origin. Possibly derived from Medieval Latin baga (“ring”), from Old Saxon bāg, bōg (“ring, ornament”), from Proto-Germanic *baugaz (“ring, bracelet, armband”); or possibly the Anglo-Norman word is derived from an earlier, unattested English word (compare Old English bēag (“ring, bracelet, collar, crown”). Cognate with Scots bagie, badgie, bawgy (“badge”).

ex.en: Each boy student has a school badge on his cap.
ex.ja: 男子生徒のめいめいが帽子に学校のバッジをつけています。

ex.en: It's a badge of honor.
ex.ja: 名誉の証です。

ex.en: Has anyone seen my badge?
ex.ja: 誰か僕のバッジ見なかった？

note.ja: 中英語 bage から。語源ははっきりしない。「記章・バッジ」。

en: Strangely unconventional; highly unusual and different from common experience, often in an extravagant, fantastic, and/or conspicuous way.
A carnation having stripes of two distinct colours on the white petals.
A tulip with a certain pattern of various colored stripes.

bizarre.ety: Borrowed from French bizarre (“odd, peculiar, bizarre”, formerly “headlong, angry”), then either from Italian bizzarro (“weird, eccentric, frisky”) or, less likely, from Basque bizar (literally “beard”, from the notion that bearded Spanish soldiers made a strange impression on the French).

ex.en: I wonder who this bizarre law is for.
ex.ja: こんな変な法律誰のためにあるんだろう。

ex.en: It's a very bizarre animal.
ex.ja: これは非常に奇怪な動物です。

note.ja: フランス語 bizarre（風変わりな）から。イタリア語 bizzarro（怒りっぽい）にさかのぼるとされる。

en: To change the direction of motion after hitting an obstacle.
To move quickly up and then down (or vice versa), once or repeatedly.
A change of direction of motion after hitting the ground or an obstacle.
A movement up and then down (or vice versa), once or repeatedly.

bounce.ety:
From Middle English bounsen, bunsen (“to beat, thump”), cognate with Scots bunce, bonce (“to bounce”). Of uncertain origin. Perhaps imitative, related to bump, or related to Middle English bonchen (“to pound, beat”) and Dutch bonken (“to bump”).
Compare Saterland Frisian bumzje (“to pound, bang, bounce”), West Frisian bûnzje (“to throb, bounce, pulsate”), Dutch bonzen (“to thump, knock, throb, bounce”), German Low German bunsen, bumsen (“to beat, bounce”), German bumsen (“to thud, bang, pound”).

ex.en: The ball bounced high in the air.
ex.ja: ボールは空中高く跳ね上がった。

ex.en: The ball bounced over the wall.
ex.ja: 球はバウンドして塀を越えた。

ex.en: That's the way the ball bounces.
ex.ja: ボールはそういうふうにはねるもの。

note.ja: 中英語 bunsen（打つ）から。擬音的な語。「弾む・跳ね返る」→ 小切手が「不渡りになる」。

en: A complete assembly, consisting of an artillery tube and a breech mechanism, firing mechanism or base cap, which is a component of a gun,…
Any similar device for shooting material out of a tube.
To bombard with cannons.
To play the carom billiard shot; to strike two balls with the cue ball.

cannon.ety: Attested from around 1400 as Middle English canon, canoun, from Old French canon, from Italian cannone, from Latin canna, from Ancient Greek κάννα (kánna, “reed”), from Akkadian 𒄀 (qanû, “reed”), from Sumerian 𒄀𒈾 (gi.na) (for more, see cane). Doublet of canyon. This spelling was not fixed until about 1800.

ex.en: The cannon went off by accident.
ex.ja: 大砲が偶然発射してしまった。

ex.en: That warship armed with eight cannons is a "Queen Elizabeth" class.
ex.ja: その大砲8門を備えた軍艦の船級は「クイーンエリザベス」です。

note.ja: イタリア語 cannone（大きな筒）から。canna（葦・筒）+ 拡大の -one。cane（杖）、canal（運河）と同系。

en: A round dance accompanied by singing.
A ballad or song of joy.
To participate in a carol (a round dance accompanied by singing).
To sing in a joyful manner.

carol.ety:
The noun is derived from Middle English carole (“round dance with singing; group of people dancing and singing in a circle; song by carollers, carol; religious poem or song; circular thing; braid, chain (?); stall for study or writing; writing table”), from Old French carole (“round dance with singing”). ex.en: Carol has been studying Spanish for three years.
ex.ja: キャロルはスペイン語を３年間勉強しつづけている。

ex.en: Carol will have left for London by eight tomorrow.
ex.ja: キャロルは明日の８時までにロンドンへ出発してしまっているだろう。

ex.en: Carol refused; in other words her answer was "no."
ex.ja: キャロルは拒絶した。言い換えると、彼女の答えは「ノー」だった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 carole（輪舞・歌）から。「祝い歌」→「クリスマスキャロル」。

en: The state of being complex; intricacy; entanglement.
That which is and renders complex; intricacy; complication.

complexity.ety: From complex + -ity. Partially displaced native English manifoldness.

ex.en: He dwelt on the complexities of modern life.
ex.ja: 彼は現代生活の複雑性について長々と話した。

ex.en: It cannot plausibly be argued that behaviour of such complexity derives entirely from instinct.
ex.ja: そのような複雑な行動が本能のみに由来するという主張はとうてい成り立たない。

note.ja: complex（複雑な）+ -ity。complex は com（共に）+ plectere（編む）。「いろいろ編み合わさった」→「複雑」。

en: The act of consulting.
A conference for the exchange of information and advice.

consultation.ety: From Middle French consultation, from Latin consultatio. Morphologically consult + -ation.

ex.en: I had a consultation with a lawyer about my will.
ex.ja: 私は遺言のことで弁護士と相談した。

ex.en: I'd like to have a consultation about getting braces.
ex.ja: 歯列矯正についてご相談したいのですが。

note.ja: consult（相談する）+ ation。→「相談・協議・診察」。

en: The quality of being convenient.
Any object that makes life more convenient; a helpful item.
To make convenient.

convenience.ety: Borrowed from Latin convenientia, from conveniens (“suitable”), present participle of convenire (“to come together, suit”). Doublet of convenance.

ex.en: Please do the work at your own convenience.
ex.ja: あなたのご都合の良い時にその仕事をして下さい。

ex.en: I live close to a convenience store.
ex.ja: 私はコンビニエンスストアの近くに住んでいます。

ex.en: Tom works at a convenience store near my house.
ex.ja: トムは家の近くのコンビニで働いてるんだ。

note.ja: con（共に）+ veni（来る）+ ence。うまく合ってやって来ること →「便利さ・好都合」。convenience store は「コンビニ」。

en: Intentionally, or after deliberation; not accidentally.
Taking one's time, slowly and carefully.

ex.en: He deliberately exposed her to danger.
ex.ja: 彼は故意に彼女を危険にさらした。

ex.en: He deliberately broke the glass.
ex.ja: 彼は故意にコップを割った。

ex.en: She deliberately ignored me on the street.
ex.ja: 彼女はわざと通りで私のことを無視した。

note.ja: deliberate（熟慮した）+ -ly。de（十分に）+ librare（はかりで量る）。libra（天秤）。「よく量って」→「慎重に → わざと」。

A synchronic dictionary of a standardised language held to only contain words that are properly part of the language.
To look up in a dictionary.
To add to a dictionary.

ex.en: What did you buy this expensive dictionary for?
ex.ja: 何のために君はこの高価な辞書を買ったのか。

en: The state of being dignified or worthy of esteem: elevation of mind or character.
Decorum, formality, stateliness.

dignity.ety: Inherited from Middle English dignyte, from Old French dignité, from Latin dignitās (“worthiness, merit, dignity, grandeur, authority, rank, office”), from dignus (“worthy, appropriate”), from Proto-Italic *degnos, from Proto-Indo-European *dḱ-nos, from *deḱ- (“to take”). See also decus (“honor, esteem”) and decet (“it is fitting”). Cognate to deign. Doublet of dainty. In this sense, displaced native Old English weorþsċipe, which became Modern English worship. It also displaced native Old English hād (“honor, dignity”).

ex.en: You don't have proper dignity as chief of the section.
ex.ja: 君は課長としての貫禄がないね。

ex.en: He said that with dignity.
ex.ja: 彼はそれを威厳をもって言った。

ex.en: It is beneath my dignity to ask a favor.
ex.ja: 恩恵を請うのは私の威厳に関わる。

note.ja: ラテン語 dignus（ふさわしい・価値ある）から。「価値があること」→「尊厳・威厳」。deign（〜してくださる）、indignant（憤慨した）も同じ。

en: The self, especially with a sense of self-importance.
The most central part of the mind, which mediates with one's surroundings.

Borrowed from Latin ego (“I”). Chosen by Freud’s translator as a translation of his use of German Ich as a noun for this concept from the pronoun ich (“I”). Doublet of I and Ich.

ex.en: I'm often told I have a strong ego.
ex.ja: よく「自我が強い」と言われます。

ex.en: He doesn't want to lose his ego.
ex.ja: 彼は自我を失うことを望んでいない。

ex.en: This problem is the clash of the idol's and obsessive fan's egos.
ex.ja: この問題は、アイドルのエゴとヲタのエゴの衝突だ。

note.ja: ラテン語で「私」。→「自我」→「うぬぼれ」。egoist（利己主義者）。

en: An intensity of feeling; an excited interest or eagerness.
Something in which one is keenly interested.

enthusiasm.ety: First attested from 1603, from Middle French enthousiasme, from Late Latin enthusiasmus, from Ancient Greek ἐνθουσιασμός (enthousiasmós), from ἐν (en, “in”) + θεός (theós, “god”) + οὐσία (ousía, “essence”).

ex.en: I saw her at it with great enthusiasm.
ex.ja: 私は彼女が熱心にやっているところを見た。

ex.en: They must have failed through lack of enthusiasm.
ex.ja: 彼らは熱意が足りないために失敗したにちがいない。

ex.en: Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
ex.ja: いまだかつて偉大なもので熱烈な精神なくして成し遂げられたものは何もない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 en（中に）+ theos（神）。「神が中に宿った状態」→「熱狂・熱意」。theology（神学）。

en: The act or process of equating two or more things, or the state of those things being equal (that is, identical).
An assertion that two expressions are equal, expressed by writing the two expressions separated by an equal sign; in mathematical problem…

equation.ety:
From Old French, from Latin aequātiō (“an equalizing”).
Morphologically equate + -ion

ex.en: Find the solution to the following equation.
ex.ja: 以下の方程式の解を求めよ。

ex.en: Solve the cubic equation x³ + 2x² − x − 2 = 0.
ex.ja: 3次方程式 x³ + 2x² − x − 2 = 0 を解け。

ex.en: Even my tutor couldn't solve this equation.
ex.ja: 私のチューターでさえこの方程式は解けなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 aequare（等しくする）から。equal（等しい）と同じ。「等しいとする式」→「方程式」。

en: Something that is extracted or drawn out.
A portion of a book, document, recording etc. incorporated distinctly in another work (for written or spoken words, synonymous to a citat…
To draw out; to pull out; to remove forcibly from a fixed position, as by traction or suction, etc.
To withdraw by squeezing, distillation, or other mechanical or chemical process. Compare abstract (transitive verb).

extract.ety: Borrowed from Latin extractum, neuter perfect passive participle of extrahō, from ex- (“out of”) + trahō (“to drag”).

ex.en: DNA is extracted from a blood sample.
ex.ja: ＤＮＡは血液のサンプルから取れる。

ex.en: The newspaper extracted several passages from the speech.
ex.ja: 新聞はその演説から数箇所引用していた。

ex.en: Should I have my tooth extracted?
ex.ja: 抜歯しなければなりませんか。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ tract（引く）。外へ引き出す →「抽出する・引用・エキス」。

en: To carry; transport; convey.
To move someone or something from one place to another, usually repeatedly.
A boat or ship used to transport people, smaller vehicles and goods from one port to another, usually on a regular schedule.
A place where passengers are transported across water in such a ship.

ferry.ety:
The verb is from Middle English ferien (“to carry, convey”), from Old English ferian, from Proto-West Germanic *farjan, from Proto-Germanic *farjaną, which see for cognates. This verb is the causative of Proto-Germanic *faraną (“to go, travel”), whence English fare; ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *per-.
The noun is from Middle English ferie (“place of crossing, ferry”), which was derived from the above verb under influence of Old Norse ferja, from Proto-Germanic *farjǭ, itself also from the verb.
False cognate of Latin ferō.

ex.en: They run a ferry service across the river.
ex.ja: その川にはフェリーの便がある。

ex.en: A big wave turned the ferry over.
ex.ja: 大波がフェリーを転覆させた。

ex.en: I took the ferry because I went by car.
ex.ja: 車だったから、フェリーに乗ったんだ。

note.ja: 古英語 ferian（運ぶ）から。fare（運賃・行く）と同系。「人を運ぶ船」→「フェリー」。

en: A person who catches fish, especially for a living or for sport; a person engaging in the pastime of fishing.

fisher.ety: From Middle English fischer, fischare, from Old English fisċere (“fisher”), from Proto-Germanic *fiskārijaz (“fisher”), equivalent to fish + -er. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Fisker (“fisher”), West Frisian fisker (“fisher”), Dutch visser (“fisher”), German Low German Fisker, Fisser (“fisher”), German Fischer (“fisher”), Danish fisker (“fisher”), Swedish fiskare (“fisher”).

ex.en: This is the boy whose name is Tom Fisher.
ex.ja: こちらがトム・フィッシャーという名前の男の子です。

note.ja: fish + -er（〜する人）。「魚を捕る人」→「漁師」。fisherman と同じ。

en: The quality of being flexible, whether physically or metaphorically.
The quality of having options.

flexibility.ety: From French flexibilité, from Late Latin flexibilitās, from Latin flectō (“to bend, curve”). Equivalent to flexible + -ity = flex + -ibility.

ex.en: Lack of flexibility is an obstacle to progress.
ex.ja: 柔軟性の欠如は進歩の障害となる。

ex.en: Lack of flexibility is an obstacle to one's progress.
ex.ja: 柔軟性の欠如は進歩の障害となる。

note.ja: flex（曲げる）+ ibility。曲げられる性質 →「柔軟性」。

en: A refrigerator.
To place (something) inside a refrigerator to chill; to refrigerate.

fridge.ety:
The noun is a clipping of refrigerator, perhaps influenced by the Frigidaire brand of refrigerators, or frigerator (“(dated) refrigerator”). The spelling is likely influenced by analogy with bridge, ridge, etc. The verb is derived from the noun.
The fandom slang verb sense alludes to the phrase "women in refrigerators" coined by the American comic book writer Gail Simone. Simone was referencing a plot point in Green Lantern (volume 3, issue 54, 1994), in which the Green Lantern's girlfriend is murdered by a villain, and her body placed in a refrigerator for him to find.

ex.en: There is no meat left in the fridge.
ex.ja: 冷蔵庫には肉は残っていません。

ex.en: Is there anything to drink in the fridge?
ex.ja: 冷蔵庫に飲み物はありますか？

ex.en: How many eggs are there in the fridge?
ex.ja: 冷蔵庫に卵いくつある？

note.ja: refrigerator を短くした語。re（再び）+ frigus（寒さ）。frigid（極寒の）。

en: The act of merging separate things, or the result thereof.
A nuclear reaction in which nuclei combine to form more massive nuclei with the concomitant release of energy.

fusion.ety: First appears c. 1555, in a translation by Richard Eden. From Middle French fusion, from Latin fūsiōnem (the accusative of fūsiō), from fusus, past participle of fundō (“to pour; to melt”) (see also found). Doublet of foison.

ex.en: The physicist was aware of the potential danger of nuclear fusion.
ex.ja: その物理学者は核融合の潜在的な危険性に気づいていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 fundere（注ぐ・溶かす）から。fus + ion。溶けて一つになること →「融合・核融合」。

en: A measure; a standard of measure; an instrument to determine dimensions, distance, or capacity; a standard
An act of measuring.
To measure or determine with a gauge; to measure the capacity of.
To estimate.

gauge.ety: From Middle English gauge, gaugen, from Anglo-Norman, Old Northern French gauger (compare Modern French jauger from Old French jaugier), from gauge (“gauging rod”), from Frankish *galgā (“measuring rod, pole”), from Proto-Germanic *galgô (“pole, stake, cross”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰalgʰ-, *ǵʰalg- (“perch, long switch”). Cognate with Old High German galgo, Old Frisian galga, Old English ġealga (“cross-beam, gallows”), Old Norse galgi (“cross-beam, gallows”), Old Norse gelgja (“pole, perch”). Doublet of gallows.

ex.en: For instance, gauges, such as thermometers and barometers, are instruments.
ex.ja: 例えば、温度計や気圧計などの計器は器具です。

note.ja: 古北フランス語 gauge（計量の基準）から。「測る基準」→「計器・尺度・規格（線路の幅など）」。

en: Any ruminant of the genus Capra.
The meat of these animals.
To allow goats to feed on.
To scapegoat.

goat.ety:
Inherited from Middle English goot, got, gat, from Old English gāt, from Proto-West Germanic *gait, from Proto-Germanic *gaits, from a substrate language.
The sense of lecherous man derives from the slang expression “horny as a goat”.

ex.en: Can you tell a sheep from a goat?
ex.ja: 羊と山羊の区別がわかりますか。

ex.en: Not hardly. He eats like a goat.
ex.ja: そんなことないですよ。何でも食べますから。

ex.en: A politician like that gets my goat.
ex.ja: ああいう政治家を見るといらいらする。

note.ja: 古英語 gāt から。北欧語・ドイツ語 Geiß と同じゲルマン系の語。

en: The alimentary canal, especially the intestine.
The abdomen of a person, especially one that is enlarged.
To eviscerate.
To remove or destroy the vital parts of.
Made of gut.
Instinctive.

gut.ety:
From Middle English gut, gutte, gotte, from Old English gutt (usually in plural guttas (“guts, entrails”)), from Proto-Germanic *gut-, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰewd- (“to pour”). Related to English gote (“drain”), Old English ġēotan (“to pour”). More at gote, yote.
The verb is from Middle English gutten, gotten (“to gut”).

ex.en: It takes real guts to start a fight.
ex.ja: 手ェ出すたぁ、いい度胸だ。

ex.en: I'm a person with guts and a strong will.
ex.ja: 私にはガッツとやる気があります。

ex.en: You've got a lot of guts.
ex.ja: 君はすごく根性があるね。

note.ja: 古英語 guttas（腸）から。「腸」→（guts）「根性」→「直感的な」（gut feeling）。

en: A hard, protective head covering, typically part of armour.
The upper part of a chemist's retort.
To cover with, or as if with, a helmet.

helmet.ety: From Middle English helmet, helmett, a borrowing from Old French helmet, heaumet, a diminutive of helme (Modern French heaume), equivalent to helm + -et. The Old French is itself of Germanic origin (whence Old English helm). Used in English since the 15th century, it has largely displaced helm as the general word.

ex.en: You have to wear a helmet to protect your head.
ex.ja: 頭を保護するためにはヘルメットをかぶらなくてはいけない。

ex.en: Tom has told Mary she needs to wear a helmet.
ex.ja: トムは、ヘルメットをかぶる必要があるとメアリーに言った。

ex.en: Tom told Mary that she needs to wear a helmet.
ex.ja: トムは、ヘルメットをかぶる必要があるとメアリーに言った。

note.ja: 古フランス語 helme（かぶと）+ 縮小の -et。helm（かぶと）はゲルマン系で「覆うもの」。

en: Doctrine, philosophy, body of beliefs or principles belonging to an individual or group.
The study of the origin and nature of ideas.

ideology.ety: Borrowed from French idéologie, from idéo- + -logie (equivalent to English ideo- + -logy). Cognate with, but not derived from, idea. Coined 1796 by Antoine Destutt de Tracy. Modern sense of “doctrine” attributed to use of related idéologue (“ideologue”) by Napoleon Bonaparte as a term of abuse towards political opponents in early 1800s.

ex.en: This is the ideology to which my speech is written.
ex.ja: これが私の固執しているイデオロギーだ。

ex.en: It goes without saying that the ideology is behind the times.
ex.ja: 言うまでもないことだが、その思想は時代遅れだ。

ex.en: We came to the conclusion that the ideology was behind the times.
ex.ja: 私たちの達した結論は、その政治思想は時代遅れであるということだった。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 idea（形・考え）+ -logy（学）。もとは「観念の学問」→「思想体系・イデオロギー」。

en: An addition or annex to a group, set, or total.
The act of including, i.e. adding or annexing, (something) to a group, set, or total.

inclusion.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₁én
Proto-Italic *en
Proto-Italic *en-
Latin in-
Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂w-der.
Proto-Italic *klaudō
Latin claudō
Latin inclūdō
Proto-Indo-European *-tis
Proto-Indo-European *-Hō
Proto-Indo-European *-tiHō
Proto-Italic *-tiō
Latin -tiō
Latin inclūsiōbor.
English inclusion
Borrowed from Latin inclūsiō, inclūsiōnis, from the verb Latin inclūdō (“to shut in, enclose, insert”), from in- (“in”) + claudō (“to shut”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂w- (“key, hook, nail”). By surface analysis, include + -sion. Doublet of enclosure.

note.ja: in（中へ）+ clus（閉じる）+ ion。中に閉じ込めること →「含むこと・包含」。

en: An arthropod (in the Insecta class) characterized by six legs, up to four wings, and a chitinous exoskeleton.

insect.ety: Borrowed from Middle French insecte, from Latin īnsectum, from īnsectus (“cut into, cut up, with a notched or divided body”), from perfect passive participle of īnsecō (“to cut into, to cut up”), from in- + secō (“to cut”), from the notion that the insect's body is "cut into" three sections (head, thorax, abdomen). Calque of Ancient Greek ἔντομον (éntomon, “insect”), from ἔντομος (éntomos, “cut into pieces”).

ex.en: What do you call this insect in English?
ex.ja: 英語でこの昆虫を何といいますか。

ex.en: I am interested in the study of insects.
ex.ja: 私は昆虫の研究に興味がある。

ex.en: If you look carefully, you'll find some insects.
ex.ja: 注意深く観察すれば、昆虫がいることがわかるだろう。

note.ja: in（中に）+ sect（切る）。体に切れ目が入っている生き物 →「昆虫」。

en: One who instructs; a teacher.

instructor.ety: From Latin instructor, equivalent to instruct + -or.

ex.en: My driving instructor says I should be more patient.
ex.ja: 教習所の教師にそう焦るなと言われています。

ex.en: I know an English language instructor who comes from Canada.
ex.ja: 私はカナダ出身の英語の先生を知っています。

ex.en: The instructor advised me to get exercise every day.
ex.ja: 教官は私に毎日運動するように勧めた。

note.ja: instruct（教える）+ -or。in（中に）+ struere（積み上げる・組み立てる）。「頭の中に知識を組み立てる人」。structure、construct も同じ。

en: The state of being isolated, detached, or separated; the state of being away from other people.
The act of isolating.

isolation.ety: First attested in 1800. From French isolation, from isolé, placed on an island (thus away from other people). Equivalent to isolate + -ion.

ex.en: Isolation is the common lot of man.
ex.ja: 孤独は人間共通の運命だ。

ex.en: We shouldn't confuse solitude with isolation. They are two separate things.
ex.ja: 孤独と孤立を混同してはいけない。それぞれ異なったものである。

note.ja: isolate（孤立させる）+ -ion。イタリア語 isolato（島になった）から、insula（島）。「島のように切り離すこと」。peninsula と同じ。

en: One who keeps (retains) something.
One who remains or keeps in a place or position.

keeper.ety: From Middle English kepere. By surface analysis, keep + -er.

ex.en: Finders keepers, losers weepers.
ex.ja: 見つけた人がもらう人、なくした人は泣きをみる。

note.ja: keep（保つ・守る）+ -er。「守る人」→「番人・管理人・ゴールキーパー」。

en: A young sheep; especially, one younger than nine months.
The flesh of a lamb used as food; (sometimes loosely) the flesh of a sheep of any age used as food.
Of a sheep, to give birth.
To assist (sheep) to give birth.

lamb.ety:
From Middle English lamb, from Old English lamb, from Proto-West Germanic *lamb, from Proto-Germanic *lambaz, probably from Proto-Indo-European *h₁l̥h₁onbʰos, enlargement of *h₁elh₁én, ultimately from *h₁el-.
See also Dutch lam, German Lamm, Bavarian Lamperl, Danish lam, Swedish lamm, Finnish lammas, Scottish Gaelic lon (“elk”), Ancient Greek ἔλαφος (élaphos, “red deer”). More at elk.

ex.en: The lamb was killed by the wolf.
ex.ja: 子羊は狼に殺された。

ex.en: This child is as gentle as a lamb today.
ex.ja: この子は今日、借りてきた猫のようだ。

ex.en: They keep lambs for meat in Arabia.
ex.ja: アラビアでは肉をとるために小羊を飼っている。

note.ja: 古英語 lamb から。ドイツ語 Lamm と同じゲルマン系の語。

en: Someone who tells a lie; especially, a person who frequently lies.

liar.ety: Inherited from Middle English lier, liere, lyere, liȝer, lieȝer, legher, from Old English lēgere, lēogere (“liar, false witness, hypocrite”), from Proto-West Germanic *leugārī, from Proto-Germanic *leugārijaz (“liar”), from *leuganą (“to lie”) + *-ārijaz, equivalent to lie + -ar. More at lie.

ex.en: I was made out to be a liar.
ex.ja: 嘘吐きものにされちゃった。

ex.en: He was looked down on as a liar.
ex.ja: 彼はうそつきだと軽蔑された。

ex.en: He made me out to be a liar.
ex.ja: 彼は僕をうそつきであるかのように言った。

note.ja: lie（うそをつく）+ -ar。「うそをつく人」。lie（横たわる）とは別語。

en: The machines constituting a production apparatus, in a plant etc., collectively.
The working parts of a machine as a group.

ex.en: Our factory needs a lot of machinery.
ex.ja: 我々の工場にはたくさんの機械が必要だ。

ex.en: Something must be wrong with the machinery.
ex.ja: どこか機構が悪いに違いない。

ex.en: The machinery was produced by American company.
ex.ja: その機械はアメリカの会社が作った。

note.ja: machine（機械）+ -ery（集合）。「機械をまとめて」→「機械類・仕組み」。machine はギリシャ語 mēchanē（仕掛け）、mechanism と同じ。

en: A large luxurious house or building, usually built for the wealthy.
A luxurious flat (apartment).

mansion.ety: Inherited from Middle English mansioun, borrowed from Anglo-Norman mansion, mansiun, from Latin mānsiō (“dwelling, stopping-place”), from the past participle stem of manēre (“stay”). By surface analysis, manse + -ion.

ex.en: She lives in quite a big mansion.
ex.ja: 彼女はちょっとした邸宅に住んでいる。

ex.en: He was very rich, and therefore could buy a mansion.
ex.ja: 彼は金持ちだった、だから大邸宅が買えた。

ex.en: They live in a mansion.
ex.ja: 彼らは大邸宅に住んでいる。

note.ja: ラテン語 manere（とどまる）から。「住む所」→「大邸宅」。remain（残る）、permanent も同じ manere。日本語の「マンション」（集合住宅）とは意味が違うので注意。

en: A silvery-coloured, metallic chemical element with the atomic number 80; it is liquid at room temperature, and toxic.
Preceded by the: mercury (noun sense 1) as used in the column of a barometer or thermometer, its fall or rise thus indicating the decreas…
To apply or coat (something) with mercury (noun sense 1) or a preparation containing mercury.
To administer to (someone) a medicine containing mercury.

mercury.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin Mercurius
Latin mercuriusder.
Middle English mercurie
English mercury
The noun is derived from Middle English mercurie (“metallic chemical element, quicksilver; a plant, probably goosefoot (genus Chenopodium); (possibly) dog’s mercury (Mercurialis perennis); etc.”), borrowed from Late Latin mercurius (“metallic chemical element, quicksilver”), Latin Mercurius (“Mercury, the Roman god of commerce, communication, etc.; the planet Mercury; etc.”), possibly from merc-, a stem of merx (“goods, wares; merchandise”); further etymology uncertain, possibly:
* from Etruscan; or
* fr

ex.en: Mercury is the planet nearest to the sun.
ex.ja: 水星は太陽に一番近い惑星です。

ex.en: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun.
ex.ja: 水星は太陽に一番近い惑星です。

ex.en: Mercury is the closest planet to the sun.
ex.ja: 水星は太陽に一番近い惑星です。

note.ja: ローマ神話の商売と使者の神 Mercurius から。足の速い神 → 素早く動く液体金属 →「水銀」、太陽の周りを速く回る →「水星」。merchant（商人）と同系とされる。

en: Specifically; that is to say.
Notable, distinguished; famous, renowned; well-known.

namely.ety: From Middle English namely, nameliche, namelike, equivalent to name + -ly. Cognate with Saterland Frisian nämmelk, West Frisian nammentlik, Dutch namelijk, German Low German nämlich, German nämlich, Danish nemlig, Swedish nämligen, Icelandic nefnilega.

ex.en: It was due a week ago, namely on April second.
ex.ja: それは１週間前、すなわち４月２日に行われた。

note.ja: name（名前）+ -ly。「名前を挙げると」→「すなわち」。

en: Awaiting a conclusion or a confirmation.
Begun but not completed.
While waiting for something; until.
During.

ex.en: We postponed our picnic pending a change in the weather.
ex.ja: 我々は天気が変わるまでピクニックを延ばした。

note.ja: フランス語 pendant（ぶら下がっている間）から、ラテン語 pendere（ぶら下がる）。「宙ぶらりんの」→「未決定の」。pendant、depend も同じ。

en: The chemical element with atomic number 78 and symbol Pt; a dense, malleable, ductile, highly unreactive, silverish-white transition meta…
A whitish grey colour, like that of the metal.
Of a whitish grey colour, like that of the metal.
Of a musical recording that has sold over one million copies (for singles), or two million (for albums).
To attain all of the achievements in a game (originally on certain PlayStation consoles, now colloquially used regardless of platform).

platinum.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *pleth₂-
Proto-Indo-European *-us
Proto-Indo-European *pléth₂us
Proto-Hellenic *plətús
Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús)bor.
Vulgar Latin *plattusder.
Spanish plata
Proto-Indo-European *-nós
Proto-Indo-European *-iHnos
Proto-Italic *-īnos
Latin -īnus
Spanish -ina
Spanish platina
English -um
English platinum
From Spanish platina (“little silver”) del Pinto ("of the Pinto") + -um. It was called "little" (or "lesser") silver because the metal was found as an impurity in gold, and del Pinto for the Pinto River in Gran Colombia where Europeans discovered it being mine

note.ja: スペイン語 platina（小さな銀）から。plata（銀）+ 縮小。「銀に似た金属」。

en: To have (something) as, or as if as, an owner; to have, to own.
Of an idea, thought, etc.: to dominate (someone's mind); to strongly influence.

possess.ety:
PIE word
 *pótis
From Middle English possessen (“to have, own; to obtain possession of; to inhabit, occupy”) [and other forms], from Middle French possesser, possessier, Old French possesser, possessier (“to have, own, possess; to dominate”), from Latin possessus (“possessed; seized”), the perfect passive participle of possideō (“to have, hold, own, possess; to have possessions; to take control or possession of, occupy, seize; to abide, inhabit, occupy; to dominate”), from potis (“able, capable, possible”) (from Proto-Indo-European *pótis (“master; ruler; husband”)) + sedeō (“to sit; to be sea

ex.en: I possess three kinds of video-game machines.
ex.ja: 私は３種類のビデオゲーム機を持っている。

ex.en: Man is the only animal that possesses language.
ex.ja: 人間は言葉を持つ唯一の動物である。

ex.en: He possessed a large house and two cars.
ex.ja: 彼は大きな家と車を２台持っていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 possidere（力をもって座る）から。poss（力がある）+ ess。→「所有する・取りつく」。

en: A proposition antecedently supposed or proved; something previously stated or assumed as the basis of further argument; a condition; a su…
Any of the first propositions of a syllogism, from which the conclusion is deduced.
To state or assume something as a proposition to an argument.
To make a premise.

premise.ety:
From Middle English premise, premisse, from Old French premisse, from Medieval Latin premissa (“set before”) (premissa propositio (“the proposition set before”)), feminine past participle of Latin praemittere (“to send or put before”), from prae- (“before”) + mittere (“to send”).
Sense 4, a piece of real estate arose from the misinterpretation of the word by property owners while reading title deeds where the word was used with the legal sense.

ex.en: You ought to think over whether the premise is valid or not.
ex.ja: その前提が妥当かどうかよく考えるべきだ。

ex.en: Life is the art of drawing sufficient conclusions from insufficient premises.
ex.ja: 人生とは不十分な前提から十分な結論を引き出す技術である。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ mis（送る）+ e。前もって送り出された（言明）→「前提」、複数形 premises は（証書で先に述べられた）「敷地・建物」。

en: The state of being probable.
An event that is likely to occur.

probability.ety: From Middle French probabilité, from Latin probābilitās (“probability, credibility”), from probābilis (“probable, credible”).

ex.en: In all probability, we shall arrive before them.
ex.ja: きっと私たちの方が彼らよりも前に到着するだろう。

ex.en: In all probability, we'll arrive before they do.
ex.ja: きっと私たちの方が彼らよりも前に到着するだろう。

ex.en: In all probability, the cabinet will fall.
ex.ja: たぶんその内閣はつぶれるでしょう。

note.ja: probable（ありそうな）+ -ity。ラテン語 probare（試す・証明する）から。「証明できそうな度合い」→「確率」。prove と同じ。

en: The act of resigning.
A written or oral declaration that one resigns.

resignation.ety: From Middle English resignacion, resignacioun, from Old French resignation, from Medieval Latin resignātiōnem, accusative of resignātio. Equivalent to resign + -ation.

ex.en: He handed in his resignation to his boss.
ex.ja: 彼は上司に辞表を提出した。

ex.en: Resignation is the first lesson of life.
ex.ja: 何事も諦めが肝心だ。

ex.en: There is an air of resignation everywhere.
ex.ja: どこに行ってもどうしようもないという感じになっていますね。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ sign（印）+ ation。署名して地位を返すこと →「辞任・辞表・あきらめ」。

en: An old Dutch gold coin with the figure of a man on horseback stamped upon it.
Someone who rides a horse or (later) a bicycle, motorcycle etc.

rider.ety: From Middle English ryder, ridere, from Late Old English rīdere (“rider, knight”). Compare Dutch rijder, German Reiter. By surface analysis, ride + -er.

ex.en: The prancing chestnut mare whinnied as she tried to get rid of the rider.
ex.ja: 棹立ちした栗毛の牝馬は嘶き、騎手を落とそうとした。

note.ja: ride（乗る）+ -er。「乗り手」。road（道）も同じ ride から。

en: Related to a rite or repeated set of actions.
A rite; a repeated set of actions, especially in religious contexts (that is, a service).

ritual.ety: From Latin rītuālis (adjective), from rītus (“rite”) + -ālis. Displaced native Old English ġewuna and wuna.

ex.en: Some people dislike the traditional New Year's ritual.
ex.ja: 正月の伝統的な行事が嫌いな人もある。

ex.en: Rituals were performed in churches.
ex.ja: 教会では儀式が執り行われた。

ex.en: A sacred ritual took place in the magnificent temple.
ex.ja: 神聖な儀式がその荘厳な寺院で執り行われた。

note.ja: ラテン語 ritus（儀式）から。rite（儀式）+ -al。

A sudden impact or blow.
The shock and noise produced by violently closing a door or other object.

slam.ety: From Middle English *slammen (not recorded), apparently from a Scandinavian source ultimately from Old Norse slæma, slœma (“to slam, swing a weapon, strike an object out of reach”), related to Old Norse slamra, slambra (“to slam”). Cognate with Norwegian Bokmål slamre (“to slam”), Swedish slamra (“to pound, beat, make a clatter, rattle”), Norwegian Nynorsk slamra (“to sway, dangle”).

ex.ja: 彼は私の鼻先でドアをぱたんとしめた。

ex.ja: ドアのパタンという音がきこえた。

To sign; to mark with one's signature as a token of consent or attestation.

en: An imagined superior type of human being representing a new stage of human development; an übermensch; (loosely), a man of extraordinary …
Someone likened to the comics character Superman; a man of seemingly superhuman powers.

superman.ety:
A calque of German Übermensch; super- + man. The German word was introduced by the philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche (1844–1900) in his work Also sprach Zarathustra (Thus Spoke Zarathustra, 1883), and rendered in English as superman by Irish playwright George Bernard Shaw (1856–1950) in the play Man and Superman (1903) and by Thomas Common (1850–1919) in his 1909 translation of Nietzsche’s work.
The “person of extraordinary powers” sense was reinforced by the DC Comics’ character Superman, who first appeared in Action Comics #1 dated June 1938.

ex.en: "Superman" is showing at the movie theatre this month.
ex.ja: 「スーパーマン」は今月その映画館で上映中です。

ex.en: "Superman" is showing at the movie theater this month.
ex.ja: 「スーパーマン」は今月その映画館で上映中です。

ex.en: Superman flies as fast as a rocket.
ex.ja: スーパーマンはロケットと同じくらいに速く飛ぶ。

note.ja: super（超えて）+ man。ニーチェの Übermensch の英訳として広まった。「人を超えた者」→「超人」。

voltage.ety: From volt + -age, ultimately derived from the name of Alessandro Volta, inventor of the modern battery.

ex.ja: バッテリーの電圧が低くなってきた。

note.ja: volt（ボルト）+ -age（状態・量を表す接尾辞）。volt は電池を発明したイタリアの物理学者ボルタ（Volta）の名前から →「電圧」。

en: The state of being wide.
The measurement of the extent of something from side to side.

Replaced Middle English wide, wyde (“width”).

ex.ja: その道路は幅が１０フィートだ。

ex.ja: この道の幅はどれくらいですか。

note.ja: wide（広い）+ -th（名詞化）。「広さ」→「幅」。length（long）、depth（deep）と同じ作り。

Release from imprisonment on payment of such money.
To secure the release of an arrested person by providing bail.
To release a person under such guarantee.

bail.ety: From Middle English baille, from the Old French verb bailler (“to deliver or hand over”) and noun bail (“lease”), from Latin bāiulāre (“carry or bear”), from baiulus (“porter; steward”) (English: bailiff).

ex.en: Tom disappeared while out on bail.
ex.ja: トムは保釈中に行方をくらました。

ex.en: Leonid was released on bail.
ex.ja: レオニードは保釈された。

ex.en: Sulphuric acid was formally referred to as Melanterite oil.
ex.ja: 硫酸は古くは「緑礬油」と呼ばれていた。

en: A female deity.
An incredibly beautiful, gorgeous, sexy, attractive woman honored and adored for her beauty or of superior charm and intelligence.

goddess.ety: From Middle English goddesse, equivalent to god + -ess, formed about 1350. The figurative meaning is first found in Edmund Spenser's Shepheardes calender (1579). Displaced Old English gyden.

ex.en: The Romans worshiped their goddess, Juno.
ex.ja: ローマ人は彼らの女神であるジューノを崇拝した。

note.ja: god（神）+ -ess（女性形）。actress、princess と同じ -ess。

en: Persistent attacks and criticism causing worry and distress.
Deliberate pestering or intimidation.

harassment.ety: Borrowed from Middle French harassement. By surface analysis, harass + -ment.

ex.en: Sexual harassment has now become a social issue.
ex.ja: セクシャルハラスメントはいまや社会問題となった。

ex.en: Women's rights groups are going after sexual harassment.
ex.ja: 女性の権利を主張する団体はセクハラ問題を追求しています。

ex.en: I wonder if you can sue someone of the same sex for sexual harassment?
ex.ja: 同性をセクハラで訴えることできないのかしら。

note.ja: harass（悩ませる）+ -ment。古フランス語 harer（犬をけしかける）から。「しつこく追い立てること」→「嫌がらせ」。

en: To put in between or into.
An image inserted into text.
A promotional or instructive leaflet inserted into a magazine, newspaper, tape or disk package, etc.

insert.ety: From Latin insertus, past participle of inserō, from in- + serō (“join, bind together, connect, entwine, interweave”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ser- (“to bind, put together, to line up”). Compare exsert.

ex.en: He inserted the key in the lock.
ex.ja: 彼は鍵を鍵穴に差し込んだ。

ex.en: I am holding a glass bottle with a letter inserted.
ex.ja: 手紙を入れたガラスびんを持っている。

ex.en: The secretary inserted the letter in the envelope.
ex.ja: 秘書は手紙を封筒の中に差し込んだ。

note.ja: in（中に）+ serere（つなぐ・並べる）。「中に差し入れてつなぐ」→「挿入する」。series（連続）、assert（主張する）も同じ。

en: Legitimate; legal; allowed by the rules; valid.
Not using cheats.
Legitimately; within the law.

note.ja: legitimate（正当な）の短縮。ラテン語 lex（法）。legal と同じ。

en: A liquid obtained by cooking meat or vegetables (or both).
A parsley sauce commonly served with traditional pies and mash.
To drink liquor, usually to excess.
To cause someone to drink liquor, usually to excess.

liquor.ety: From Middle English licour, from Anglo-Norman licour, from Latin liquor (“fluidity, liquidness, a fluid, a liquid”), from liquere (“to be fluid or liquid”); see liquid. Doublet of liqueur.

ex.en: Liquor will have an effect on a person.
ex.ja: お酒を飲むと影響が出るものだ。

ex.en: He is the owner of the liquor shop.
ex.ja: 彼があそこの酒屋の主人です。

ex.en: Liquor is not sold at this store.
ex.ja: この店では酒類は売っていない。

note.ja: ラテン語 liquor（液体）から。liquid と同じ。「液体」→「酒」。

en: A person who loses; one who fails to win or thrive.
Something of poor quality.

loser.ety: From Middle English loser, losere, equivalent to lose + -er. In the sense of contemptible or worthless individual, perhaps an alteration of losel, which see.

ex.en: He is a good loser.
ex.ja: 彼は諦めが早い。

ex.en: Tom thinks I'm a loser.
ex.ja: トムは私のことを負け犬だと思っている。

ex.en: Stop hanging out with losers.
ex.ja: 負け犬とつるむな。

note.ja: lose（失う・負ける）+ -er。「負けた人」→「敗者・負け犬」。

en: The action of rubbing, kneading or hitting someone's body, to help the person relax, prepare for muscular action (as in contact sports) o…
The action of rubbing or kneading anything.
To rub and knead (someone's body or body part), to perform a massage on (somebody).
To rub or knead anything.

massage.ety: From French massage (noun), from masser (“to massage”) (borrowed around the end of the 18th century from Arabic مَسَّ (massa, “feel, touch”), or from Portuguese amassar) + -age. Cognate to German massieren.

ex.en: Would you like me to massage your chest?
ex.ja: 胸をさすってあげましょうか。

ex.en: He asked for a back massage.
ex.ja: 彼は背中のマッサージを頼んだ。

ex.en: I feel good just by watching someone get a massage.
ex.ja: マッサージされてるのを見るだけで気持ちよくなる。

note.ja: フランス語 massage から。masser（もむ）、アラビア語 massa（触る）にさかのぼるとされる。

en: A son of one's sibling, brother-in-law, or sister-in-law; either a son of one's brother (fraternal nephew) or a son of one's sister (soro…
A son of one's cousin or cousin-in-law

nephew.ety: From Middle English nevew, neveu (“nephew, grandson”), from Old French neveu, from Latin nepos, nepōtem, from Proto-Italic *nepōts (“nephew, grandson”), whence also French neveu, Italian nipote. Displaced or absorbed the inherited English neve (“nephew, grandson, male cousin”), from Middle English neve, from Old English nefa, from Proto-West Germanic *nefō, from Proto-Germanic *nefô (“nephew, grandson”), whence Dutch neef, German Neffe. All ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *népōts (“grandchild, sister's son”). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian nećak, Irish nia, Persian نوه (nave). Doublet of neve

ex.en: He is not my son, but my nephew.
ex.ja: 彼は私の息子ではなく、甥である。

ex.en: All her money went to her nephew.
ex.ja: 彼女の金はすべておいのものとなった。

ex.en: A nephew is a son of one's brother or sister.
ex.ja: 甥とは兄弟か姉妹の息子のことです。

note.ja: ラテン語 nepos（孫・甥）から。nepotism（縁故主義：身内をひいきする）も同じ。

en: As a pointed example; in a notable manner.

notably.ety: From Middle English notably, notabili, notablelyche, equivalent to notable + -ly.

note.ja: notable（注目すべき）+ -ly。「特に・著しく」。note と同じ。

en: A large group of musicians who play together on various instruments, usually including some from strings, woodwind, brass and/or percussi…
A semicircular space in front of the stage used by the chorus in Ancient Greek and Hellenistic theatres.

orchestra.ety: Borrowed from Latin orchēstra, borrowed from Ancient Greek ὀρχήστρα (orkhḗstra), from ὀρχέομαι (orkhéomai, “to dance”) + -τρᾰ (-tră, “a suffix used to form instrument nouns (pl.)”).

ex.en: This is the fifth concert by this orchestra.
ex.ja: これはオーケストラの５回目の演奏会です。

ex.en: All the orchestra were pleased with their success.
ex.ja: オーケストラの楽団員はみな成功を喜んだ。

ex.en: I'm going to join the school orchestra.
ex.ja: 学校のオーケストラに入るつもりなのだ。

note.ja: 古代ギリシャの劇場で、舞台前の合唱隊が踊る半円の場所 orkhēstra（orkheisthai 踊る）。→ そこにいる演奏者の集団 →「管弦楽団」。

en: A flattened mass of anything soft, to sit or lie on.
A cushion used as a saddle without a tree or frame.
To stuff.
To furnish with a pad or padding.
Indicating a soft flat sound, as of bare footsteps.

pad.ety: 1554, "bundle of straw to lie on". Unknown, and unclear whether all senses have a common etymology. For sense "ends of a digit", cf. Low German or West Flemish pad (“sole of the foot”), perhaps ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pent- (“to pass”), which would make it related to both path and find.

ex.en: A woman is taking down some notes on a pad of paper.
ex.ja: 女性が何かを書き留めている。

ex.en: May I use your ink pad?
ex.ja: 朱肉をお借りしてもよろしいですか。

ex.en: The rockets were fired from a launching pad.
ex.ja: ロケットは発射台から打ち上げられた。

note.ja: 「詰め物」が原義とされる。クッション →「当て物・パッド」、紙を重ねて綴じたもの →「メモ帳」、足裏のクッション →「肉球」。

en: A person from Pakistan or of Pakistani descent.
Of, from, or pertaining to Pakistan, or its people.

en: The state of being precise or exact; especially, both exact and accurate.
The ability of a measurement to be reproduced consistently.
Used for exact or precise measurement.
Made, or characterized by accuracy.

precision.ety: From Middle French precision. Equivalent to precise + -ion.

ex.en: Flawless precision is required in the measurements.
ex.ja: 測定には寸分の狂いもない精度が要求される。

ex.en: Precision in measurement is a necessity.
ex.ja: 測定においては正確さは欠かせないものである。

ex.en: He copied his friend's notebook with precision.
ex.ja: 彼は友達のノートを正確に写した。

note.ja: precise（正確な）+ -ion。prae（前もって）+ caedere（切る）。「前もってきっちり切りそろえた」→「精密さ」。decide（切り離す → 決める）も同じ caedere。

en: The act of preserving; care to preserve; act of keeping from destruction, decay or any ill.
The state of being preserved, how something has survived.

preservation.ety: From Old French preservacion, from Medieval Latin preservatio. Morphologically preserve + -ation.

ex.en: Sleep is essential for the preservation of life.
ex.ja: 生きていくのにはどうしても眠ることが不可欠だ。

ex.en: He has dedicated his life to the preservation of nature.
ex.ja: 彼は一生を自然保護のためにささげた。

note.ja: pre（前もって）+ serv（保つ）+ ation。→「保存・保護」。

ex.en: He contrived a means of speaking to Nancy privately.
ex.ja: 彼はナンシーと２人だけで話す手段を考えた。

note.ja: private（私的な）+ -ly。「個人的に・内密に」。ラテン語 privatus（公から離れた）。

en: A statement or claim of questionable accuracy, from no known reliable source, usually spread by word of mouth.
Information or misinformation of the kind contained in such claims.
To tell a rumor about; to gossip.

rumor.ety: From Middle English rumour, from Old French rumeur, from Latin rūmor (“common talk”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃rewH- (“to shout, to roar”).

ex.en: The rumor may or may not be true.
ex.ja: そのうわさは本当かもしれないし、本当でないかもしれない。

ex.en: Who is at the bottom of these rumors?
ex.ja: このうわさの張本人はだれだ？

ex.en: The rumor proved to be an absolute lie.
ex.ja: うわさは全くのうそであることがわかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 rumor（ざわめき・うわさ）から。

en: A piece of fabric attached to a boat and arranged such that it causes the wind to drive the boat along. The sail may be attached to the b…
The concept of a sail or sails, as if a substance.
To be impelled or driven forward by the action of wind upon sails, as a ship on water; to be impelled on a body of water by steam or othe…
To move through or on the water; to swim, as a fish or a waterfowl.

sail.ety: From Middle English saile, sayle, seil, seyl, from Old English seġl, from Proto-West Germanic *segl, from Proto-Germanic *seglą. Cognate with West Frisian seil, Low German Segel, Dutch zeil, German Segel, Danish sejl, Swedish segel.

ex.en: There was a ship sailing on the sea.
ex.ja: 一隻の船が海を走っていた。

ex.en: They sailed along the west coast of Africa.
ex.ja: 彼らはアフリカの西海岸に沿って航海した。

ex.en: The boat sailed across the Pacific Ocean.
ex.ja: その船は太平洋を横断した。

note.ja: 古英語 segl から。ゲルマン系の語。「帆」→「帆走する・航海する」。

en: One of several species of fish, typically of the Salmoninae subfamily, brownish above with silvery sides and delicate pinkish-orange fles…
A meal or dish made from this fish.
Having a pale pinkish-orange colour.

salmon.ety:
From Middle English samoun, samon, saumon, from Anglo-Norman saumon, from Old French saumon, from Latin salmō, salmōn-. Widely displaced native Middle English lax, from Old English leax (whence modern dialectal lax). The unpronounced l was later inserted to make the word appear closer to its Latin root (compare words like debt, indict, receipt for the same spelling Latinizations).
The verb sense “ride a bicycle the wrong way down a one-way street” alludes to salmon swimming upstream against the flow of a river to spawn.

ex.en: Salmon lay their eggs in fresh water.
ex.ja: サケは淡水で産卵する。

ex.en: This is a salmon that came up the river.
ex.ja: これはその川をのぼってきたサケです。

ex.en: Give me three pieces of salmon.
ex.ja: 鮭を３切れ下さい。

note.ja: ラテン語 salmo から。salire（跳ぶ）と関係するとされ、川をさかのぼって跳ねる魚。salient（突き出た）。l は発音しない。

en: In secret, covertly.

secretly.ety:
Etymology tree
English secret
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English secretly
From secret + -ly.

ex.en: I think Tom and Mary are secretly married.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーはひそかに結婚していると思う。

ex.en: What have you two been secretly up to?
ex.ja: さっきから何を二人でこそこそやってるの？

ex.en: I know who you're secretly in love with.
ex.ja: あなたが密かに想いを寄せてる人が誰か知ってるよ。

note.ja: secret（秘密）+ -ly。secret は se（離れて）+ cernere（分ける）。「分けて隠しておく」。secretary（秘書：秘密を預かる人）。

en: Someone who sells; a vendor; a clerk.
Something which sells.

seller.ety: From Middle English seller, sellere, (also siller, sullar, sullere), from Old English *sellere, *syllere, equivalent to sell + -er (agent noun) (sense 1) and sell + -er (patient) (sense 2). Cognate with Danish sælger, Swedish säljare, Icelandic seljari (“a seller; dealer”).

ex.en: This book ought to be a good seller.
ex.ja: この本はよく売れるはずだ。

ex.en: When goods are scarce, sellers have the advantage.
ex.ja: 品物が少ないときには売り手が有利だ。

ex.en: This book, which was once a best seller, is now out of print.
ex.ja: この本はかつてはベストセラーだったが、今は絶版になっている。

note.ja: sell（売る）+ -er。「売り手」→ よく売れる物 →「best seller」。

en: Very thin or transparent.
Downright; complete; pure.
A sheer curtain or fabric.
To swerve from a course.

sheer.ety:
From Middle English shere, scheere, schere, skere, from Old English sċǣre (“pure, sheer; shining, clear”), from Proto-Germanic *skairiz; supplanted the semantically close shire (dialectal), from Middle English schyre, schire, shire, shir, from Old English sċīr (“clear, bright; brilliant, gleaming, shining, splendid, resplendent; pure”), beside which existed Middle English skyr, from Old Norse skírr (“pure, bright, clear”), both from Proto-Germanic *skīriz (“pure, sheer”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ḱeh₁y- (“luster, gloss, shadow”).
Cognate with Danish skær, German schier (“sheer”), German Lo

ex.en: Her success was due to sheer hard work.
ex.ja: 彼女の成功は全くの熱心な努力のおかげであった。

ex.en: It is a sheer waste of time.
ex.ja: それは全くの時間の浪費だ。

ex.en: He ran sheer into the wall.
ex.ja: 彼はもろに壁にぶつかった。

note.ja: 「混じりけのない・澄んだ」が原義。→「まったくの」、まっすぐ澄んで落ちる →「切り立った」、透けるほど →「ごく薄い」。

en: For a special purpose, person, or occasion.
Extremely.

specially.ety: From Middle English specialli, specially, equivalent to special + -ly.

ex.en: This is a store that caters specially to students.
ex.ja: これは学生相手の店です。

ex.en: The stage he specially prepared was wasted.
ex.ja: せっかく彼が用意した舞台を台無しにしてしまった。

note.ja: special（特別な）+ -ly。ラテン語 species（種類・外見）から。「ある種類だけの」→「特別な」。specific も同じ。

en: A feeling of pity or sorrow for the suffering or distress of another.
The formal expression of pity or sorrow for someone else's misfortune.

sympathy.ety: Borrowed from Middle French sympathie, from Late Latin sympathīa (“feeling in common”), from Ancient Greek σῠμπᾰ́θειᾰ (sŭmpắtheiă, “fellow feeling”), from σῠμπᾰθής (sŭmpăthḗs, “affected by like feelings; exerting mutual influence, interacting”) + -ῐᾰ (-ĭă, “-y”, nominal suffix). Equivalent to sym- (“acting or considered together”) + -pathy (“feeling”).

ex.en: We have a lot of sympathies in common.
ex.ja: 我々は共鳴する点がおおい。

ex.en: I feel sympathy for people with that disease.
ex.ja: 私はその病気にかかった人に同情する。

ex.en: I could not help feeling sympathy with him.
ex.ja: 私は彼に同情せざるをえなかった。

note.ja: sym（共に）+ path（感じる）+ y。共に感じること →「同情・共感」。telepathy（遠くで感じる）も同じ path。

en: A light, brown-like colour.
A darkening of the skin resulting from exposure to sunlight or similar light sources.
Yellowish-brown.
Having dark skin as a result of exposure to the sun or an artificial process intended to mimic this effect.
To change to a tan colour due to exposure to the sun.
To change an animal hide into leather by soaking it in tannic acid.

tan.ety: From Middle English tan, from Old French tan (“tanbark”), from Gaulish *tannos (“green oak”) – compare Breton tann (“red oak”), Old Cornish tannen –, from Proto-Celtic *tannos (“green oak”), of uncertain origin, but perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *(s)dʰonu (“fir”). Per this hypothesis, related to Hittite [script needed] (tanau, “fir”), Latin femur, genitive feminis (“thigh”), German Tann (“woods”), Tanne (“fir”), Albanian thanë (“cranberry bush”), Ancient Greek θάμνος (thámnos, “thicket”), Avestan 𐬚𐬀𐬥𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬭𐬆 (θanuuar^ə), Sanskrit धनु (dhánu).

ex.en: I plan to get a nice tan this summer.
ex.ja: この夏はこんがり焼こうと思います。

ex.en: I tanned myself on the beach.
ex.ja: 私は浜辺で肌を焼いた。

ex.en: I was browned to a nice tan.
ex.ja: 私はこんがりと小麦色に日焼けした。

note.ja: ラテン語 tannum（なめし用の樫の樹皮）から。皮をなめすと茶色になる →「黄褐色」→「日焼けする」。

en: Of or relating to theory; abstract; not empirical.

theoretical.ety: From Middle English theorothycall, probably from Latin theōrēticus + -al, from Ancient Greek θεωρητικός (theōrētikós).

ex.en: That shows his theoretical background.
ex.ja: それは彼の理論的背景を示している。

ex.en: This manual is too theoretical and not very practical.
ex.ja: このマニュアルは理論的すぎて、あまり実用的ではない。

ex.en: The Greeks made theoretical models of geometry.
ex.ja: ギリシャ人たちは幾何学の理論的原形を作った。

note.ja: theory（理論）+ -ical。ギリシャ語 theōria（眺めること・観察）、theatre（見る場所）と同じ。「よく眺めて組み立てた考え」。

ja: （thumb through で）ぱらぱらめくる

en: The shortest and thickest digit of the hand that for humans has the most mobility and can be made to oppose (moved to touch) all of the o…
The part of a slider that may be moved linearly along the slider.
To touch or cover with the thumb.
To turn the pages of (a book) in order to read it cursorily.

thumb.ety:
Derived from Middle English thombe, thoume, thoumbe (“thumb”), from Old English þūma (“thumb”), from Proto-West Germanic *þūmō (“thumb”), from Proto-Germanic *þūmô (“thumb”), from Proto-Indo-European *tūm- (“to grow”).
Cognate with West Frisian tomme (“thumb”), Dutch duim (“thumb”), Low German Duum (“thumb”), German Daumen (“thumb”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk tomme (“inch”), Norn tum (“thumb”), Swedish tumme (“thumb”), tum (“inch”), Russian дюйм (djujm, “inch”), Ancient Greek τύμβος (túmbos, “burial mound”). Also compare Welsh tyfu (“to grow”), Latin tumēre (“to swell”),

ex.en: When I was a kid, I was all thumbs.
ex.ja: 私は子供の頃不器用だった。

ex.en: When it comes to making things, I'm all thumbs.
ex.ja: 物を作るとなると、私は不器用です。

ex.en: I'm all thumbs in the kitchen.
ex.ja: 私は炊事が全然できない。

note.ja: 古英語 thūma から。「太い（指）」が原義とされる。tumor（腫れ）とも同系の印欧祖語にさかのぼる。

en: Trees in a forest regarded as a source of wood.
Wood that has been pre-cut and is ready for use in construction.
Used by loggers to warn others that a tree being felled is falling.
A cry used when anything is falling over.
To fit with timbers.
To light or land on a tree.

timber.ety:
From Middle English tymber, from Old English timber, from Proto-West Germanic *timr, from Proto-Germanic *timrą (“building; timber”), from Proto-Indo-European *dem- (“to build; to arrange”) (see Proto-Indo-European *dṓm (“home, house”)).
Cognates

ex.en: Large amounts of timber are used in paper making.
ex.ja: 大量の材木が紙の製造に使われている。

ex.en: Canada abounds in timber.
ex.ja: カナダは木材に富む。

note.ja: 古英語 timber（建材・家）から。ドイツ語 Zimmer（部屋）と同じ語源。「家を建てる材料」→「材木」。

en: See-through, clear; having the property that light passes through it almost undisturbed, such that one can see through it clearly.
Of a graphical image or animated GIF, having parts that allow the background to show through.
Something that is transparent.

transparent.ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin trānspārēns, trānspārēntis (“transparent”), present participle of transpareō, from Latin trans + pareō. Displaced native Old English þurhsīene.

ex.en: This transparent liquid contains a kind of poison.
ex.ja: この透明な液体は毒のようなものを含んでいる。

ex.en: This transparent liquid contains poison.
ex.ja: この透明な液体には毒が含まれている。

note.ja: trans（通して）+ pare（見える）+ nt。向こうまで透けて見える →「透明な・明白な」。

en: The highest or uppermost side or portion of something.
A favourable aspect of something that also has an unfavourable aspect.
On the top of.

ex.en: All our things were turned upside down.
ex.ja: 我々の道具は全部ひっくり返された。

ex.en: Take care not to turn the box upside down.
ex.ja: その箱をひっくりかえさないように注意してくれ。

ex.en: I turned the table upside down to fix it.
ex.ja: 私は修理するためにテーブルを上下にひっくり返した。

note.ja: up + side。「上側」→「利点」。upside down（逆さまに）。

preceding a word or its initial letter, to imply that the referent benefits health or wellness

ex.en: Tom decided that it wasn't necessary to take vitamins.
ex.ja: トムはビタミン剤を飲む必要はないと判断した。

ex.en: This diet is full of vitamins.
ex.ja: この食事にはビタミンがたくさんはいっている。

ex.en: You should eat some vegetables rich in vitamins.
ex.ja: ビタミンが豊富にある野菜を食べた方がいい。

en: Containing nothing; empty; not occupied or filled.
Having no incumbent; unoccupied; said of offices etc.
An empty space; a vacuum.
An extended region of space containing no galaxies.
To make invalid or worthless.
Synonym of empty (verb).

void.ety: From Middle English voide, voyde, from Old French vuit, voide, vuide (modern vide), in turn from Vulgar Latin *vocitum, ultimately from Latin vacuus.

ex.en: The will was declared void by the court.
ex.ja: その遺言は法廷で無効と宣告された。

ex.en: Her words were wholly void of meaning.
ex.ja: 彼女の言葉はまったく無意味だった。

ex.en: This bond is null and void.
ex.ja: この証書は完全に無効である。

note.ja: ラテン語 vocivus / vacuus（空の）から。→「空っぽの・無効の・空間」。avoid（避ける）も同じ。

en: Done, given, or acting of one's own free will.
Done by design or intention; intentional.
A short piece of music, often having improvisation, played on a solo instrument.
A volunteer.

voluntary.ety: From Middle English voluntarie, from Old French volontaire, from Latin voluntārius (“willing, of free will”), from voluntās (“will, choice, desire”), from volēns, present participle of volo (“to will”). Displaced native Old English selfwille (literally “self-willed”).

ex.en: He made a voluntary contribution to the school.
ex.ja: 彼はその学校に自発的に寄付した。

ex.en: She did a lot of voluntary work for the Red Cross.
ex.ja: 彼女は赤十字のために自発的な労働をたくさんした。

ex.en: That organization depends on voluntary contributions.
ex.ja: その組織の運営は自発的な寄付に依存している。

note.ja: ラテン語 voluntas（意志）から。volo（〜したい）。「自分の意志で」→「自発的な」。volunteer も同じ。

en: Any of the several cereal grains, of the genus Triticum, that yields flour as used in bakery.
A light brown color, like that of wheat.
Wheaten, of a light brown color, like that of wheat.

wheat.ety: From Middle English whete, from Old English hwǣte, from Proto-West Germanic *hwaitī, from Proto-Germanic *hwaitijaz (compare West Frisian weet, Dutch weit, Low German Weten, German Weizen, Danish hvede, Swedish vete, Norwegian Bokmål hvete, Norwegian Nynorsk kveite, Faroese and Icelandic hveiti), from *hwītaz (“white”). More at white.

ex.en: The buildings are filled with bags of wheat.
ex.ja: 建物は小麦の袋で一杯です。

ex.en: The wheat is coming very well this year.
ex.ja: 今年は小麦がよく育っている。

ex.en: His family had been wheat farmers.
ex.ja: 彼の家族は小麦農家だった。

note.ja: 古英語 hwǣte から。white（白い）と同系で「白い粉になる穀物」。

en: A lash; a pliant, flexible instrument, such as a rod (commonly of cane or rattan) or a plaited or braided rope or thong (commonly of leat…
The same instrument used to strike a person or animal for corporal punishment or torture.
To hit with a whip.
To hit with any flexible object.

whip.ety:
From Middle English whippen, wippen (“to flap violently”), from Middle Dutch wippen (“to swing, leap, dance, oscillate”) and Middle Low German wippen (“to move quickly”), from Proto-Germanic *wippōną (“to move back and forth”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *weyp- (“to shake; to swing”). (See Swedish vippa and Danish vippe (“to shake”)).
The unetymological wh- is probably expressive of the sound of a whip; compare the same development in whisk and onomatopoeias such as whack and whoosh.
The political senses are from whipper-in (“huntsman who keeps the hounds from wandering”), from 18th-c

ex.en: If you eat any cake, I'll whip you.
ex.ja: もしケーキをひとつでも食べたら、ぶつからね。

ex.en: I'm sure you'll whip us up something really good.
ex.ja: 期待しているから。

ex.en: The new boss has whipped the company into shape.
ex.ja: 新社長は、会社の体質を堅固なものに作り上げた。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 wippen（揺れる・振る）と関係する語。「さっと振る」→「むち・むちで打つ」→（卵などを）泡立てる。

en: To move an object over, maintaining contact, with the intention of removing some substance from the surface. (Compare rub.)
To smear (a substance) with this kind of motion.
The act of wiping something.
A soft piece of cloth or cloth-like material used for wiping.

wipe.ety: From Middle English wipen, from Old English wīpian (“to wipe, rub, cleanse”), from Proto-West Germanic *wīpōn (“to wipe”), from Proto-Indo-European *weyp- (“to twist, wind around”). Cognate with German wippen (“to bob”), Swedish veva (“to turn, wind, crank”), Gothic 𐍅𐌴𐌹𐍀𐌰𐌽 (weipan, “to wreathe, crown”), Old English swīfan (“to revolve, sweep, wend, intervene”), Sanskrit वेपते (vépate, “to tremble”). More at swivel, swift.

ex.en: The population of the town was wiped out.
ex.ja: その町の住民は全滅した。

ex.en: Would you like me to wipe your body?
ex.ja: 体をふいてあげましょうか。

ex.en: Would you wipe the table for me?
ex.ja: テーブルをふいてくれませんか。

note.ja: 古英語 wīpian（拭く）から。「拭く」→「拭い去る・消去する」。

en: The complex joint between forearm bones, carpus, and metacarpals where the hand is attached to the arm; the carpus in a narrow sense.
A stud or pin which forms a journal.
To hit a wrist shot.

wrist.ety: From Middle English wrist, from Old English wrist, from Proto-West Germanic *wristu, from Proto-Germanic *wristuz (compare Old Frisian wrist, Low German Wrist, German Rist (“back of hand, instep, withers”), Swedish vrist), from Proto-Germanic *wrīþaną (“to twist, turn”). More at writhe.

ex.en: The man caught the girl by the wrist.
ex.ja: その男は少女の手首をつかんだ。

ex.en: I broke my wrist when I fell on it.
ex.ja: 転んだ時、手首を折った。

ex.en: I fell down and hurt my wrist.
ex.ja: 転んで手首を痛めました。

note.ja: 古英語 wrist から。「ねじる所」が原義で、wrest（ねじり取る）、wrestle（取っ組み合う）と同系。

en: Brief, quick, short.
High or shrill.
A person who has the acute form of a disorder, such as schizophrenia.
An accent or tone higher than others.
To give an acute sound to.

acute.ety:
From Late Middle English acute (“of a disease or fever: starting suddenly and lasting for a short time; of a humour: irritating, sharp”), from Latin acūta, from acūtus (“sharp, sharpened”), perfect passive participle of acuō (“to make pointed, sharpen, whet”), from acus (“needle, pin”). The word is cognate to ague (“acute, intermittent fever”).
As regards the noun, which is derived from the verb, compare Middle English acūte (“severe but short-lived fever; of blood: corrosiveness, sharpness; musical note of high pitch”).

ex.en: A dog has an acute sense of smell.
ex.ja: イヌは鋭い嗅覚を持っている。

ex.en: He felt an acute pain in his chest.
ex.ja: 彼は胸に激痛を覚えた。

ex.en: I have an acute pain here.
ex.ja: ここに急性の痛みがあります。

note.ja: ラテン語 acuere（鋭くする）から。「とがった」→「鋭い・急性の・鋭角の」。acid（酸っぱい）、acupuncture（鍼）も同じ ac-（とがった）。

en: The commander of a naval squadron or fleet, regardless of formal rank.
The appointed commander of a navy, regardless of formal title.

ex.en: There is a statue of Admiral Nelson in Trafalgar Square.
ex.ja: トラファルガー広場にはネルソン提督の彫像がある。

en: The elongated curved tropical fruit of a banana plant, which grows in bunches and has a creamy flesh and a smooth skin.
In particular, the sweet, yellow fruit of the Cavendish banana cultivar, which may be eaten raw, as distinct from e.g. a plantain for coo…
Curved like a banana, especially of a ball in flight.

banana.ety:
Borrowed from Portuguese banana or Spanish banana, derived from a Niger-Congo language spoken in the Guinea region. Specific derivation is unclear. Possible ancestor or cognate languages include Wolof banaana, Eastern Maninkakan banana, and Vai ꕒꘌꕯ (ɓaana) or ꕒꕌꕯ (ɓaana), possibly from Arabic بَنَان (banān, “fingertip, banana”). However, Ay Baati Wolof (Munro & Gaye, 1997) posits that Wolof banaana is itself derived from Portuguese banana.
The racial slur derives from the notion that they are “Yellow (East-Asian) on the outside, but White (Westernized) on the inside”.

ex.en: I do not want any bananas at all.
ex.ja: バナナはぜんぜんほしくない。

ex.en: Is Tom eating an apple or a banana?
ex.ja: トムが食べてるのはリンゴ？それともバナナ？

ex.en: Tom can eat a banana in three seconds.
ex.ja: トムってさぁ、バナナ１本を３秒で食べれるんだよ。

note.ja: 西アフリカの言語からポルトガル語・スペイン語を経て入った語。

en: To conduct (oneself) well, or in a given way; to conform.
To act, conduct oneself in a specific manner; used with an adverbial of manner.

ex.ja: 学生であるならそのように振舞いなさい。

ex.en: Now you are a big boy, behave yourself.
ex.ja: もう大きくなったのだから、行儀良くしなさい。

ex.en: A boy your age ought to behave well.
ex.ja: おまえぐらいの年の子は行儀よくすべきだ。

note.ja: be（十分に）+ have（持つ）。「自分を（きちんと）持つ」→「振る舞う・行儀よくする」。behavior。

en: To receive (something) from somebody temporarily, expecting to return it.
To receive money from a bank or other lender under the agreement that the lender will be paid back over time.
Deviation of the path of a rolling ball from a straight line; slope; slant.
A borrow pit.

borrow.ety:
From Middle English borwen, from Old English borgian (“to borrow, lend, pledge surety for”), from Proto-West Germanic *borgōn, from Proto-Germanic *burgōną (“to pledge, take care of”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰergʰ- (“to take care”).
Cognate with Dutch borgen (“to borrow, trust”), German borgen (“to borrow, lend”), Danish borge (“to vouch”). Related to Old English beorgan (“to save, preserve”). More at bury.

ex.en: English words are often borrowed by other languages.
ex.ja: 英語の単語は他の言語にずいぶん取り入れられている。

ex.en: Would you mind if I borrowed your car?
ex.ja: 車をお借りしてもよろしいですか。

ex.en: Is it okay if I borrow these books?
ex.ja: これらの本を借りてもいいですか。

note.ja: 古英語 borgian（保証して借りる）から。borg（担保・保証）。

en: Any building or complex of buildings in which a legislature meets.
Any citadel or complex of buildings similar to the Roman Capitol, particularly Italian and Roman citadels including temples to Jupiter, J…

capitol.ety: From Middle English Capitolie, via Anglo-Norman capitolie, Old French capitoile, from Latin Capitōlium (“Capitoline Hill, its temples; any similar citadel”), from the oblique stem of caput (“head”) + -ō (noun-forming suffix) or -ōlus (“-ole”, diminutive suffix) + -ium (toponym-forming suffix). Compare Latin capitō and capitulum. As a French magistrate, via French capitoul, from Capitole, the town hall of Toulouse. Doublet of Capitolium and capitoul.

note.ja: 古代ローマのユピテル神殿 Capitolium（カピトリウムの丘）から。caput（頭）。capital（首都）と同系だが綴りが違う。

en: Of or relating to the Celts.
Of the languages spoken by Celts.

Celtic.ety: Borrowed from French celtique or Latin celticus, equivalent to Celt + -ic. First attested in the 17th century.

ex.en: The museum has a fascinating collection of Celtic artifacts.
ex.ja: その博物館にはケルト時代の文化遺産のすばらしいコレクションがある。

ex.en: That museum has a superb collection of Celtic era cultural artifacts.
ex.ja: その博物館にはケルト時代の文化遺産のすばらしいコレクションがある。

note.ja: 古代ギリシャ人が呼んだ民族名 Keltoi から。

en: The bottom of a face, (specifically) the typically jutting jawline below the mouth.
The ability to withstand being punched in the chin without being knocked out.
To perform a chin-up (exercise in which one lifts one's own weight while hanging from a bar).
To punch or hit (someone), especially on the chin (part of the body).

chin.ety:
From Middle English chyn, from Old English ċinn (“chin”), from Proto-West Germanic *kinnu, from Proto-Germanic *kinnuz (“chin”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵénus (“chin, jaw”).
Compare West Frisian/Dutch kin, Low German/German Kinn, Danish kind, Icelandic kinn, Welsh gen, Latin gena, Tocharian A śanweṃ, Ancient Greek γένυς (génus, “jaw”), Armenian ծնոտ (cnot), Persian چانه (čâne), Sanskrit हनु (hánu). Doublet of gena.

ex.en: How many chin-ups can you do, Tom?
ex.ja: トム、懸垂何回できる？

ex.en: I need to do something about this double chin.
ex.ja: この二重あごをなんとかしたいのよ。

ex.en: I hit him on the chin.
ex.ja: 彼のあごを殴ってやった。

note.ja: 古英語 cin から。ドイツ語 Kinn と同じ。ギリシャ語 genys（あご）とも同系。

en: Of, relating to, or belonging to a city, a citizen, or citizenship; municipal or civil.
Of or relating to the citizen, or of good citizenship and its rights and duties.

civic.ety: Borrowed from Latin cīvicus (“pertaining to a city or citizens”).

note.ja: ラテン語 civis（市民）から。civ + ic。→「市民の・市の」。

en: One who occupationally provides assistance by working with records, accounts, letters, etc.; an office worker.
A salesclerk; a person who serves customers in a store or market.
To act as a clerk, to perform the duties or functions of a clerk.
To assemble information about a patient during their initial assessment by actions such as a taking a detailed medical history and perfor…

clerk.ety:
From Middle English clerc, from Old English clerc, from Late Latin clēricus (“priest, clergyman, cleric”, also generally “learned man, clerk”), from Ancient Greek κληρικός (klērikós, “of the clergy”, adj. in church jargon), from κλῆρος (klêros, “lot, inheritance”, originally “shard used in casting lots”). Doublet of cleric.
Compare typologically Russian дьяк (dʹjak) (akin to дья́кон (dʹjákon)).

ex.en: There were no clerks to wait on me.
ex.ja: 私の応対をしてくれる店員がいなかった。

ex.en: He married his daughter to a bank clerk.
ex.ja: 彼は娘を銀行員にとつがせた。

ex.en: She is a clerk of the trading company.
ex.ja: 彼女は貿易会社の事務員です。

note.ja: ラテン語 clericus（聖職者）から。中世は読み書きができるのは主に聖職者 →「書記・事務員」。cleric、clergy（聖職者）と同じ。

en: Significantly; to a degree worth considering.

From considerable + -ly.

ex.en: This area has been considerably built up of late.
ex.ja: この地区は最近家がかなり建て込んできた。

ex.en: Her health seems to have improved considerably of late.
ex.ja: 彼女は最近ずいぶん健康をとりもどしたようだ。

ex.en: The situation has improved considerably compared with what it was.
ex.ja: 以前と比べると状況は随分良くなった。

note.ja: considerable（かなりの）+ -ly。consider（よく考える）から。「考慮に値するほど」→「かなり」。

en: A small house.
A seasonal home of any size or stature, a recreational home or a home in a remote location.
To stay at a seasonal home, to go cottaging.
To have homosexual sex in a public lavatory; to practice cottaging.

cottage.ety:
Late Middle English, from Anglo-Norman cotage and Medieval Latin cotagium, from Old Northern French cot, cote (“cottage, hut”) + -age (“surrounding property”), from Old Norse kot, from Proto-Germanic *kutą, *kuta- (“shed”), probably of non-Indo-European origin, possibly borrowed from Proto-Finno-Ugric/Proto-Uralic *kota (“hut, tent”), probably akin to Proto-Iranian *kátah (“house; roof”). However, also compare Dutch and English hut.

Cognate with Saterland Frisian Koate (“cottage, hut, small house”), Dutch kot (“ramshackle housing”), German Kate, Kote (“cot, cottage, hut”), Norwegian B

ex.en: There stands a cottage close to the forest.
ex.ja: 森の近くに一軒家がある。

ex.en: Tell me what cottage cheese is made from.
ex.ja: カッテージチーズは何からできてるか教えて。

ex.en: There is a cottage beyond the bridge.
ex.ja: 橋の向こうに小屋がある。

note.ja: cot（小屋）+ -age。「小屋の住まい」→「小さな家・コテージ」。

en: A quick, brilliant, and highly successful act.
Of Native Americans, a blow against an enemy delivered in a way that demonstrates bravery.
To execute a coup.
To subject (a nation) to a coup d'état.

coup.ety: Reborrowed in modern times from modern French coup (“blow, strike”), from Old French coup, colp, from Late Latin colpus, from Latin colaphus. Doublet of cope and colpus. The same Old French word had been borrowed into Middle English as coupe, caupe (with different pronunciation).

ex.en: We only have secondhand information of the coup.
ex.ja: そのクーデターの間接的な情報しか得ていない。

ex.en: The coup attempt was foiled at the last moment.
ex.ja: クーデター計画はぎりぎりのところで阻止されました。

ex.en: The coup was meticulously executed.
ex.ja: クーデターは慎重に遂行された。

note.ja: フランス語 coup（一撃）から。coup d'état（国家への一撃）の短縮で「クーデター」→「大成功」。

en: To find fault (with something).
To evaluate (something), assessing its merits and faults.

criticize.ety: From critic + -ize; first element from Ancient Greek κριτικός (kritikós, “of or for judging, able to discern”), from κρίσις (krísis, “decision, judgement”).

ex.en: Anyone who criticizes him is asking for trouble.
ex.ja: あいつにケチをつけると後が怖い。

ex.en: Nothing is as easy as to criticize others.
ex.ja: 他人を批判するほど易しいことはない。

ex.en: It is the wrong place to criticize me.
ex.ja: オレを非難するのはお門違いだ。

note.ja: critic（批評家）+ -ize。ギリシャ語 krinein（判断する・分ける）から。crisis（分かれ目 → 危機）、criterion（判断基準）も同じ。

en: In a natural, untreated state.
Characterized by simplicity, especially something not carefully or expertly made.
Any substance in its natural state.

ex.en: The method was crude, but very effective.
ex.ja: その方法は粗雑なものであったが、効果的だった。

ex.en: The crude oil price is falling further.
ex.ja: 原油価格の値下がりが続いている。

ex.en: Crude oil has been falling in price.
ex.ja: 原油価格の値下がりが続いている。

note.ja: ラテン語 crudus（生の・血のにじむ）から。「生のまま」→「未加工の・粗野な」、未精製の石油 →「原油」。cruel（残酷な）も同じ。

en: Any of the following symbols: ‒ (figure dash), – (en dash), — (em dash), or ― (horizontal bar).
A hyphen or minus sign.
To run quickly or for a short distance.
To leave or depart.
Damn!

dash.ety: From Middle English daschen, dassen, from Danish daske (“to slap, strike”), related to Swedish daska (“to smack, slap, spank”), of obscure origin. Compare German tatschen (“to grope, paw”), Old English dwǣsċan (“to quell, put out, destroy, extinguish”). See also dush.

ex.en: The man dashed the bottle against the wall.
ex.ja: 男はビンを壁に叩きつけた。

ex.en: I must dash or I'll be late.
ex.ja: 全速力で走らなくては遅れてしまうだろう。

ex.en: A cat dashed out of the room.
ex.ja: 猫が部屋から飛び出した。

note.ja: 北欧語に由来する擬音的な語。「勢いよく打つ・投げる」→「突進する」、さっと引いた線 →「ダッシュ記号」、ぱっと加える →「少量」。

en: The act of revealing something.
The making known of a previously hidden fact or series of facts to another party; the act of disclosing.

disclosure.ety: From disclose by analogy with closure. A purely English formation.

note.ja: dis（反対）+ close（閉じる）+ -ure。「閉じていたものを開くこと」→「開示・暴露」。

ja: （at one's disposal で）自由に使えること

en: A disposition; an arrangement, categorization, or classification of things.
A kick or a handball of the ball during a game.

disposal.ety:
