ex.ja: 学生はすばらしい体育館を自由に使うことができる。

ex.en: The whole building has been put at our disposal.
ex.ja: 私達はそのビル全部を自由に使ってきた。

ex.en: This is the money at your disposal.
ex.ja: これはあなたが自由にしてよいお金です。

note.ja: dis（離して）+ pose（置く）+ -al。「離して配置する」→「処分・処理」、「自由に配置できる」→ at one's disposal（自由に使える）。dispose。

en: Distinguishing, used to or enabling the distinguishing of some thing.
Characteristic, typical.
A distinctive thing: a quality or property permitting distinguishing; a characteristic.
A distinctive accent.

distinctive.ety: From Latin distinctus, perfect passive participle of distinguere (to push apart, to divide; see distinct) + -ive (forming adjectives signifying relation or tendency to). Cognate with French distinctif and Medieval Latin distinctivus.

ex.en: Tom has a distinctive scar under his right eye.
ex.ja: トムは右目の下に独特の傷がある。

ex.en: Japan has many distinctive traits.
ex.ja: 日本には多くのはっきりとした特色がある。

ex.en: When mosquitoes beat their wings up and down, they produce a distinctive buzzing sound.
ex.ja: 蚊が羽を上下にバタバタすると、ブーンという独特の音がする。

note.ja: distinct（はっきり区別された）+ -ive。dis（離して）+ stinguere（突き刺す・印をつける）。「印をつけて区別した」→「独特の」。distinguish も同じ。

zh: 無人航空載具 /无人航空载具

en: A male hymenopteran (ant, bee, hornet, or wasp), whose sole primary function is to mate with the queen.
One who performs menial or tedious work.
To kill or destroy with a drone (unmanned aircraft), or with a missile fired by a drone.

drone.ety:
From Middle English drane, dron, drone, from Old English drān, drǣn, from Proto-West Germanic *drānu, from Proto-Germanic *drenô, *drēnuz (“drone”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰreh₁n- (“bee, drone, hornet”).
Cognates
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Droane (“drone”), Dutch dar (“drone”), German Drohne (“drone”), Limburgish dreen, Droon (“drone”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk drone (“drone”), Swedish drönare (“drone”); also Belarusian тру́цень (trúcjenʹ, “drone”), Bulgarian търтей (tărtej, “drone”), Czech trubec (“drone”), Macedonian трут (trut, “drone”), Polish trąd, trut, tru

ex.en: I want to buy a drone, but my parents won't let me.
ex.ja: ドローンを買いたいんだけど親が買わせてくれない。

ex.en: Well, unmanned drones likely lack style, right.
ex.ja: 無人機じゃ味気ないだろ。

note.ja: 古英語 drān（雄バチ）から。雄バチの羽音 →「ブーンという音」→ ブーンと飛ぶ →「無人機」。

en: A group of people or vehicles, generally armed, who go with a person or people of importance to safeguard them on a journey or mission.
An accompanying person in such a group.
To attend to in order to guard and protect; to accompany as a safeguard (for the person escorted or for others); to give honorable or cer…
To accompany (a person) in order to compel them to go somewhere (e.g. to leave a building).

escort.ety: Borrowed from French escorte, itself borrowed from Italian scorta.

ex.en: I will serve you as an escort.
ex.ja: 私が送って差し上げましょう。

ex.en: May I escort you home?
ex.ja: お宅までお送りしましょうか？

ex.en: He traveled with a large escort.
ex.ja: 彼は多数の護衛を連れて旅行した。

note.ja: イタリア語 scorta（護衛）から。ex（外へ）+ corrigere（正す）。「道を正しく導く」→「護衛する・付き添う」。correct と同じ。

en: In a firm or definite or strong manner.
Securely.

firmly.ety: From Middle English fermely; equivalent to firm + -ly.

ex.en: The event has fixed firmly in my mind.
ex.ja: その出来事がしっかりと私の心に取りついてしまった。

ex.en: I firmly believe that your time will come.
ex.ja: 私はあなたの番が来ると確信しているよ。

ex.en: This custom has become firmly established among the Japanese.
ex.ja: この習慣は日本人の間にすっかり定着した。

note.ja: firm（堅い）+ -ly。ラテン語 firmus（堅い）。confirm（確かめる）、affirm（断言する）も同じ。

en: Powder obtained by grinding or milling cereal grains, especially wheat, or other foodstuffs such as soybeans and potatoes, and used to ba…
The food made by grinding and bolting cleaned wheat (not durum or red durum) until it meets specified levels of fineness, dryness, and fr…
To apply flour to something; to cover with flour.
To reduce to flour.

flour.ety:
Spelled (until about 1830) and meaning flower in the sense of flour being the "finest portion of ground grain" (compare French fleur de farine, fine fleur). Doublet of fleur, flor, and flower. Partially displaced native meal.
The U.S. standard of identity comes from 21CFR137.105.

ex.en: He bought a lot of flour and oil.
ex.ja: 彼はたくさんの小麦粉と油を買い込んだ。

ex.en: This cake contains flour, milk, eggs and sugar.
ex.ja: このケーキには小麦粉、牛乳、卵、砂糖が含まれています。

ex.en: That flour mill is now operated as a museum.
ex.ja: その製粉場は現在博物館として運営されている。

note.ja: flower（花）と同じ語。「小麦の最良の部分（花）」→「小麦粉」。もとは同じ綴りで、後に書き分けられた。

en: Of, or relating to Hinduism, or to Hindus and their culture.
A person adhering to the Hindu religion (Hinduism).

Hindu.ety: Derived from Classical Persian هِنْدُو (hindū, “Indian, Hindu”), from Middle Persian hndwk' (Hindūg, “Indian”), from hnd (Hind, “India”), from Old Persian 𐏃𐎡𐎯𐎢 (hiⁿdu-, “India”), from Sanskrit सिन्धु (síndhu, “river, stream; Indus”), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *síndʰuṣ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *síndʰuš (“river”).

ex.en: The concept of zero comes from Hindu culture.
ex.ja: ゼロという概念は、ヒンドゥー文化に由来している。

ex.en: The concept of zero sprang from the Hindu culture.
ex.ja: ゼロという概念はヒンドゥー文化に由来している。

ex.en: Hindus do not eat beef.
ex.ja: ヒンズー教徒は牛肉を食べません。

note.ja: ペルシャ語 Hindū（インダス川の人）から。サンスクリット語 Sindhu（川・インダス川）。India も同じ。

en: Not direct
Not of obvious or immediate cause, but as a secondary result.
An indirect cost.
An indirect radiator.
To access by means of indirection; to dereference.

indirect.ety: From Middle French indirect, from Late Latin indirectus (“not direct”).

ex.en: Taxes consist of direct taxes and indirect ones.
ex.ja: 税は直接税と間接税からなっている。

ex.en: Consumption and alcohol taxes are indirect and are paid together with the cost.
ex.ja: 消費税、 酒税などは間接税で、代金と一緒に支払われる。

ex.en: New indirect taxes were imposed on spirits.
ex.ja: 新たな間接税が強い酒類に対して課せられた。

note.ja: in（否定）+ direct（まっすぐな）。「まっすぐでない」→「間接的な・遠回しの」。

en: Of, pertaining to, characteristic of, or organized along the lines of an institution.
Instituted by authority.
A client that is an organization rather than an individual.
A Chilean senator who is appointed by the president for a term of eight years.

A transitional or temporary period between other events.

ex.en: Tom has been named interim head coach.
ex.ja: トムは臨時ヘッドコーチに指名された。

ex.en: It was only supposed to be an interim solution.
ex.ja: それはただの臨時の解決策だった。

note.ja: ラテン語で「その間に」。inter（間）。「間の期間の」→「暫定的な・中間の」。

en: A sudden, often uncontrolled movement, especially of the human body.
A quick pull on something.
To make a sudden uncontrolled movement.
To give a quick, often unpleasant tug or shake.

jerk.ety: Probably from Middle English yerk (“sudden motion”) and Middle English yerkid (“tightly pulled”), from Old English ġearc (“ready, active, quick”) and Old English ġearcian (“to prepare, make ready, procure, furnish, supply”). Cognate with Scots yerk (“to jerk”). Related also to English yare (“ready”).

ex.en: Suppose there's some jerk you just can't get on with.
ex.ja: 自分と気があわない、いけ好かない、人がいるとします。

ex.en: My boss is a jerk.
ex.ja: 私のボスは最低なやつだ。

ex.en: He's such a shameless jerk.
ex.ja: 厚顔無恥とはまさにあいつのことだ。

note.ja: 擬音的な語で「さっとむち打つ・ぐいと引く」が原義。→「急な動き」→ 俗に「嫌なやつ」。

en: Having a kind personality; kind, warm-hearted, sympathetic.
In a kind manner, out of kindness.
In a favourable way.

kindly.ety: From Middle English kyndely, kyndeliche, from Old English cyndelīċ (“natural, kindly”); equivalent to kind + -ly.

ex.en: She did not take kindly to my advice.
ex.ja: 彼女は私の忠告を快く受けなかった。

ex.en: Will you kindly come here at nine?
ex.ja: 恐縮ですが、９時にここへおいで頂けますか。

ex.en: I wish I had treated the girl more kindly.
ex.ja: その少女をもっと親切に扱っておけばよかった。

note.ja: kind（親切な）+ -ly。「親切に」→ 依頼の「どうか」。

en: The state of being kind.
An instance of kind or charitable behaviour.

kindness.ety: From Middle English kyndenesse, equivalent to kind + -ness.

ex.en: I am grateful to you for your kindness.
ex.ja: ご親切を感謝しています。

ex.en: I cannot thank you enough for your kindness.
ex.ja: ご親切に対し、いくら感謝してもし過ぎることはありません。

ex.en: Thank you for your many kindnesses to me.
ex.ja: いろいろ親切にしてくれてありがとう。

note.ja: kind（親切な）+ -ness。kind はもともと「同じ生まれ・種類の（kin）」→「身内のように優しい」。kin（親族）、kind（種類）と同じ語源。

en: A scheme for the distribution of prizes by lot or chance, especially a gaming scheme in which one or more tickets bearing particular numb…
Something decided by chance.

lottery.ety: Borrowed from Italian lotteria, from the same root as Old English hlot (cognate with English lot). Compare French loterie (from Middle Dutch loterie). By surface analysis, lot + -ery.

ex.en: He won the first prize in the lottery.
ex.ja: 彼はくじ引きで一等賞を当てたよ。

ex.en: I got a camera in a lottery.
ex.ja: 福引きでカメラが当たった。

ex.en: Mary had a dream that she won the lottery.
ex.ja: メアリーは宝くじに当たる夢を見た。

note.ja: オランダ語 loterij から。lot（くじ・分け前）+ -ery。a lot of（たくさん）の lot も「くじで分けた分け前」から。

en: The absolute or relative size, extent or importance of something.
An order of magnitude.

ex.en: I hadn't realized the magnitude of the problems.
ex.ja: 私はその問題の重要さがわかっていなかった。

ex.en: He realized the magnitude of his crime.
ex.ja: 彼は犯した罪の大きさを悟った。

ex.en: I've never seen a pearl of such magnitude!
ex.ja: こんなに大きな真珠は見たことがない。

note.ja: ラテン語 magnus（大きい）から。「大きさ・規模」。magnify（拡大する）、magnificent も同じ。

en: Made less or reduced by (followed by an expression of number or quantity).
Without; deprived of.
The minus sign (−).
A negative quantity.
Being a negative quantity; pertaining to a deficit or reduction.
That is below zero by (a specified amount) on a scale.
To subtract.

minus.ety: From Middle English mynus, from Latin minus, neuter form of minor, comparative form of parvus (“small, little”), from the Proto-Indo-European root *mey- (“few, small”).

ex.en: How many is nine minus six?
ex.ja: 九引く六はいくつですか。

ex.en: The thermometer registered minus ten last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜、温度計はマイナス１０度を示した。

ex.en: The temperature went down to minus ten degrees centigrade last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜は-10℃まで冷え込んだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 minus（より少なく）から。min（小さい）。→「マイナス・〜を引いた」。

en: Without clothing or other covering of the skin; without clothing on the genitals or female nipples.
Of a color (such as beige or tan) that evokes bare flesh.
A painting, sculpture, photograph or other artwork or mass-media-reproduced image depicting one or more human figure(s) in a state of nea…
The state of total nudity.

nude.ety: Entered English 1493 as a legal term, meaning "unsupported, not formally attested," from Middle English nud, from Latin nūdus (“naked, bare”).

ex.en: What's wrong with being nude in your own house?
ex.ja: 家の中で全裸で何が悪い！

ex.en: The children were swimming in the nude.
ex.ja: 子供たちは裸で泳いでいた。

ex.en: Where are the three nude statues in the exhibition?
ex.ja: 展覧会に出ている３つの裸像がどこですか？

note.ja: ラテン語 nudus（裸の）から。naked と同系の印欧祖語にさかのぼる。

en: A vent or similar passage to allow the escape of something.
Something which allows for the release of one's desires.

outlet.ety: From Middle English outlete, outeleate, ut-lete, derived from Middle English outleten (“to allow, let out, emit”), equivalent to out- + let. Compare West Frisian útlit (“outlet”), Dutch uitlaat (“outlet”), German Auslass (“outlet”).

ex.en: Playing baseball is an outlet for energy.
ex.ja: 野球は精力のはけ口になる。

ex.en: Where can I find an outlet for all my anger?
ex.ja: この遣り場なき怒りをどこにぶつければいいのか。

ex.en: Gary found an outlet for his energy in playing football.
ex.ja: ゲーリーはフットボールをする事に活力のはけ口を見つけた。

note.ja: out（外へ）+ let（行かせる）。「外へ出す口」→「出口・はけ口・コンセント・販売店」。

en: A value kept constant during an experiment, equation, calculation, or similar, but varied over other versions of the experiment, equation…
A variable that describes a property or characteristic of some system (material, object, event, etc.) or some aspect thereof.

parameter.ety: From French paramètre, from New Latin parametrum (“parameter”), from Ancient Greek παρα- (para-, “beside”) + μέτρον (métron, “measure”).

note.ja: para（そばに）+ meter（測る）。補助として測るもの →「媒介変数・条件・範囲」。

en: To take a temporary rest, take a break for a short period after an effort.
To stop (an activity) for a while.
A temporary stop or rest; an intermission of action; interruption; suspension; cessation.
A short time for relaxing and doing something else.

pause.ety: From Middle French pause, from Latin pausa, from Ancient Greek παῦσις (paûsis), from Ancient Greek παύω (paúō, “stop”), of uncertain origin. Doublet of pausa.

ex.en: He spoke for ten minutes without a pause.
ex.ja: 彼は息もつかず１０分間話し続けた。

ex.en: The speaker paused and then went on talking again.
ex.ja: 講師は一息入れてから、また話し続けた。

ex.en: Tom paused and took a deep breath.
ex.ja: トムは止まって、深呼吸をした。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 pausis（停止）から。pauein（止める）。「止まること」→「休止」。

en: To make a solemn promise (to do something).
To deposit something as a security; to pawn.
A solemn promise to do something.
A promise to abstain from drinking alcohol.

pledge.ety: From Middle English plege, from Anglo-Norman plege, from Old French plege (Modern French pleige) from Medieval Latin plevium, plebium, from plebiō (“to pledge”), from Frankish *plehan (“to pledge; to support; to guarantee”). Akin to Old High German pflegan (“to take care of, be accustomed to”), Old Saxon plegan (“to vouch for”), Old English plēon (“to risk, endanger”). More at plight.

ex.en: She pledged herself never to do it again.
ex.ja: 彼女は二度とそんなことをしないと誓った。

ex.en: I give my pledge that I will quit smoking.
ex.ja: たばこはやめると誓います。

ex.en: He pledged to marry me when he returned home.
ex.ja: 彼は帰国したら私と結婚すると誓った。

note.ja: 古フランス語 plege（保証人・担保）から。「担保を差し出して約束する」→「誓約・公約」。

en: An entrance, entry point, or means of entry.
A large primary adit as the main entrance to a mine.
Of or relating to a porta, especially the porta of the liver.
To use a portal (magical or technological doorway).

portal.ety: From Middle English portal, porttol, from Old French portal and Medieval Latin portāle, from porta.

ex.en: What do you need to build a nether portal?
ex.ja: ネザーポータルを構築するには何が必要ですか？

note.ja: ラテン語 porta（門）から。→「（立派な）入口・玄関・ポータルサイト」。port（港）と同じ祖先。

en: A written order from an authorized medical practitioner for provision of a medicine or other treatment, such as (ophthalmology) the speci…
The medicine or treatment provided by such an order.

prescription.ety: Borrowed from Middle French, from Old French prescripcion, from Latin praescriptio (“preface; pretext; something written ahead of time”), from prae- (“pre-, before”) + scribere (“to write”) + -tio (“-tion, forming nouns”). Equivalent to prescribe + -tion.

ex.en: Go to the doctor to get your prescription!
ex.ja: 処方箋をもらうために医者に行きなさい。

ex.en: You can't buy this medicine without a prescription.
ex.ja: その薬は処方箋無しで買ってはいけません。

ex.en: To get a prescription, go to a doctor.
ex.ja: 処方箋をもらうために医者に行きなさい。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ script（書く）+ ion。前もって書いて指示したもの →「処方箋・規定」。prescribe（処方する）。

en: One who protests, either alone or in a public display of group feeling.
One who protests a bill of exchange, or note.

ex.en: Violent clashes broke out between the protesters and the police.
ex.ja: 反対派と警察の間で武力衝突が生じた。

ex.en: The protesters barricaded the entrance.
ex.ja: 抗議のデモ隊が入り口にバリケードを築いた。

note.ja: protest（抗議する）+ -er。pro（前に・公に）+ testari（証言する）。「人前ではっきり言う人」→「抗議者」。testify（証言する）。

en: Advertising or other activity designed to rouse public interest in something.
Public interest attracted in this way.

publicity.ety: From French publicité, From Medieval Latin pūblicitātem, accusative singular of pūblicitās, from Latin pūblicus (“public, general”). Morphologically public + -ity.

ex.en: The news brought her a lot of publicity.
ex.ja: そのニュースで彼女のことはみんなに広く知れ渡った。

ex.en: This event was good publicity for the company.
ex.ja: この事件は会社のいい宣伝になった。

ex.en: You're going to get much publicity with this book.
ex.ja: この本で、君はかなり評判になるよ。

note.ja: public（公の）+ -ity。ラテン語 publicus（人々の）。「人々に知られること」→「宣伝・評判」。

en: That has been the object of punishment.

ex.en: I was afraid of her having been punished.
ex.ja: 私は彼女が罰せられるのを恐れた。

ex.en: You'll be punished if you break the law.
ex.ja: 法を破れば罰せられるだろう。

ex.en: We punished him according to the rules.
ex.ja: 規則に当てはめて彼を罰した。

note.ja: punish（罰する）+ -ed。ラテン語 punire、poena（罰）。

en: A young dog, especially before sexual maturity (12–18 months).
A young rat.
To bring forth whelps or give birth to pups.

puppy.ety:
From earlier puppie (“a woman's pet dog”), of uncertain origin, but probably from Middle English *puppee, *poupee, from Old French poupée, popée (“a doll; puppet”). More at puppet.
Mostly displaced native Middle English whelp (“puppy”), from Old English hwelp, whence Modern English whelp and whelpie.

ex.en: The puppy grew larger and larger every day.
ex.ja: 子犬は日に日に大きくなった。

ex.en: I'll give these puppies to whoever likes dogs.
ex.ja: 私はこの子犬たちを犬の好きな人には誰にでもあげよう。

ex.en: I've been searching for my puppy for weeks.
ex.ja: 僕は何週間も前からうちの子犬をさがしているんだ。

note.ja: フランス語 poupée（人形）から。「かわいい小さなもの」→「子犬」。puppet（あやつり人形）と同じ語源。

en: The process or art of finding candidates for a post in an organization, or recruits for the armed forces.
A style or process of recruiting.

note.ja: recruit（募集する）+ -ment。フランス語 recroître（再び育つ）から。「軍に新しく育ってくる兵」→「新兵・新人を募集すること」。

en: A nonmetallic element (symbol Si) with an atomic number of 14 and atomic weight of 28.0855.
A single atom of this element.

silicon.ety:

ex.en: Powders of aluminium, magnesium, silicon, etc. explode.
ex.ja: アルミニウム、マグネシウム、シリコンなどの粉末が爆発する。

note.ja: ラテン語 silex（火打ち石）から。火打ち石に多く含まれる元素 →「ケイ素」。silicone（樹脂のシリコーン）とは別物。

en: That which is thin and broad.
A thin, broad piece cut off.
To cut into slices.
To cut with an edge using a drawing motion.
Having the properties of a slice knot.

slice.ety: From Middle English sclise, sklise, from Old French esclice, esclis (“a piece split off”), deverbal of esclicer, esclicier (“to splinter, split up”), from Frankish *slitjan (“to split up”), from Proto-Germanic *slitjaną, from Proto-Germanic *slītaną (“to split, tear apart”), from Proto-Indo-European *sleyd- (“to rend, injure, crumble”). Akin to Old High German sliz, gisliz (“a tear, rip”), Old High German slīȥan (“to tear”), Old English slītan (“to split up”), modern French éclisse. More at slite, slit.

ex.en: How many slices of meat would you like?
ex.ja: 肉は何切れにしましょうか。

ex.en: How many slices of pizza did you eat?
ex.ja: ピザ何切れ食べた？

ex.en: He cut off a slice of meat.
ex.ja: 彼は肉を一切れ切り取った。

note.ja: 古フランス語 esclice（木片）から。「薄く割ったもの」→「薄切り・一切れ」。

en: A rigid implement, often roughly y-shaped, that is fixed to one's heel for the purpose of prodding a horse. Often worn by, and emblematic…
A jab given with the spurs.
To prod (especially a horse) on the side or flank, with the intent to urge motion or haste, to gig.
To urge or encourage to action, or to a more vigorous pursuit of an object

spur.ety: From Middle English spure, spore, from Old English spora, spura, from Proto-West Germanic *spurō, from Proto-Germanic *spurô, from Proto-Indo-European *sperH- (“to kick”).

ex.en: More money for education will spur economic growth.
ex.ja: 教育にもっとお金をかければ、経済成長に拍車がかかるだろう。

ex.en: He says things on the spur of the moment.
ex.ja: その場限りのことを言う。

ex.en: Her desire to be a doctor spurred her on.
ex.ja: 彼女の医者になりたいと言う欲求が彼女を駆り立てた。

note.ja: 古英語 spura（拍車）から。spurn（はねつける）と同系。「馬の腹を突く金具」→「刺激・駆り立てる」。on the spur of the moment（とっさに）。

en: A person who subscribes to a publication or a service.
A system or component that subscribes to something, such as an event, made available by a publisher.

ex.en: How many subscribers does this magazine have?
ex.ja: この雑誌の発行部数はどのくらいですか。

note.ja: sub（下に）+ scrib（書く）+ er。（書類の）下に名前を書いた人 →「加入者・定期購読者」。

en: Synonym of telegraphy, any process for transmitting arbitrarily long messages over a long distance using a symbolic code.
The electrical device gradually developed in the early 19th century to transmit messages (telegrams) using Morse code; the entire system …
To use a telegraph; to send a message by telegraph.
To clearly communicate to another nonverbally (whether by gesture, a change in attitude, or any other sign), and especially unintentionally.

telegraph.ety: Borrowed from French télégraphe, equivalent to tele- (“far, distant”) + -graph (“writing”), suggested as a new name for Claude Chappe's overland semaphore network by André François Miot de Mélito in place of Chappe's original tachygraphe (“tachygraph, fast writer”).

ex.en: They telegraphed that everything was all right.
ex.ja: 彼らは万事異状なしということを電報で伝えた。

ex.en: My parents telegraphed me to come back at once.
ex.ja: 両親からすぐに帰れと電報が来た。

ex.en: The office telegraphed that they had not received my application.
ex.ja: 事務局は私の願書を受け取っていないと電報で知らせてきた。

note.ja: tele（遠く）+ graph（書く）。遠くへ書き送る仕組み →「電信・電報」。

en: Of, pertaining to, caused by, or characteristic of cowpox.
Of or pertaining to cowpox as a source of material for vaccination against smallpox; also, of or pertaining to such material used for vac…
A substance given to stimulate a body's production of antibodies and provide immunity against a disease without causing the disease itsel…
The process of vaccination; immunization, inoculation.

vaccine.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin vaccīnus (“of or derived from a cow”), from vacca (“cow (female cattle)”) + -īnus (suffix meaning ‘of or pertaining to’ forming adjectives). Sense 1 refers to the early use of the cowpox virus as a vaccination against smallpox: see New Latin variolae vaccīnae (“cowpox”, plural, literally “infectious diseases of cattle causing pustules”), coined by the British physician and scientist Edward Jenner (1749–1823).

ex.en: I haven't had the vaccine for Coronavirus.
ex.ja: コロナワクチンは打ってないです。

ex.en: I will not take the Corona vaccine.
ex.ja: コロナワクチンは受けないよ。

ex.en: I haven't had the COVID vaccine.
ex.ja: コロナワクチンは打ってないです。

note.ja: ラテン語 vacca（牛）から。牛痘（牛の天然痘）を使った種痘から名づけられた。

en: The univalent radical CH₂=CH−, derived from ethylene.
Any of various compounds and substances containing the vinyl radical, especially various tough, flexible, shiny plastics.
Containing the vinyl radical.
Made of polyvinyl chloride.

vinyl.ety:

English vinyl
From Latin vīnum (“wine”) + English -yl. Derived from Latin vīnum because ethyl alcohol is the ordinary alcohol present in wine.

ex.en: The weakness of vinyl is that it is easily affected by heat.
ex.ja: ビニールは熱に弱いのが難点だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 vinum（ワイン）+ -yl（化学の語尾）。エチルアルコールと関係する化学基の名前から。

en: In an accurate manner; exactly; precisely; without error or defect.

accurately.ety:
Etymology tree
English accurate
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English accurately
From accurate + -ly.

ex.en: He accurately described what happened there.
ex.ja: 彼はそこで起きたことを正確に描写した。

ex.en: Answer accurately in one go.
ex.ja: 一遍で正確に答えてください。

ex.en: I don't remember my grandmother's face accurately.
ex.ja: 私は祖母の顔を正確には覚えていない。

note.ja: accurate（正確な）+ -ly。ad（〜に）+ cura（注意・世話）。「注意を払った」→「正確な」。cure（治す）、care と関連。

en: Someone or something, especially, a television station, that is associated with a larger, related organization, such as a television netw…
To adopt; to receive into a family as one's offspring
to bring or receive into close connection; to ally.

affiliate.ety: From Medieval Latin affīliātus, the passive past participle of Late Latin adfīliō, affīliō (“to adopt as son”), from ad- + fīlius + -ō. Equivalent to Latin affīliō + -ate. Compare French affilié (noun).

ex.en: Our club is affiliated with an international organization.
ex.ja: 我々のクラブは国際的な組織に加入した。

ex.en: The college is affiliated with the university.
ex.ja: そのカレッジは大学に付属している。

ex.en: Why did you decide to affiliate yourself with Company A?
ex.ja: なぜ、Ａ社の傘下に入ることを選んだのか。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ filius（息子）。「養子にする」→「傘下に入れる・提携させる」。filial（子としての）。

en: A place of safety or refuge.
The protection, physical and legal, afforded by such a place (as, for example, for political refugees).

asylum.ety:

Learned borrowing from Latin asȳlum, borrowed from Ancient Greek ἄσυλον (ásulon).

ex.en: Society is an insane asylum run by the inmates.
ex.ja: 社会は患者によって運営されている精神病院です。

ex.en: The embassy denied political asylum to foreign refugees.
ex.ja: 大使館は外国人難民の政治亡命を拒否しました。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 asylon（侵されない場所）から。a（否定）+ sylē（略奪）。「略奪されない所」→「避難所・亡命」。

en: A building, often found on a farm, used for storage or keeping animals such as cattle.
A unit of surface area equal to 10⁻²⁸ square metres.
To lay up in a barn.

barn.ety:
From Middle English barn, bern, bærn, from Old English bearn, bern, contracted forms of Old English berern, bereærn (“barn, granary”), compound of bere (“barley”) and ærn, ræn (“dwelling, barn”), from Proto-West Germanic *raʀn, from Proto-Germanic *razną (compare Old Norse rann), from pre-Germanic *h₁rh̥₁-s-nó-, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁erh₁- (“to rest”).
More at rest and barley.
For the use as a unit of surface area, see w:Barn (unit) § Etymology.

ex.en: The barn was small, but it was strong.
ex.ja: その納屋は小さかったが頑丈だった。

ex.en: Don't keep the car in the barn.
ex.ja: 納屋に自動車を置いてはいけません。

ex.en: On entering the barn, he found a missing bike.
ex.ja: 納屋に入るやいなや、彼はなくなった自転車を見つけた。

note.ja: 古英語 bere（大麦）+ ærn（家）。「大麦の家」→「納屋」。

en: Relating to the office of a bishop or an archbishop.
The principal church serving as the office (and some as place of residence) of an archdiocese's/a diocese's archbishop/bishop which is sy…
A large or important church building.

cathedral.ety: From Middle English cathedral, chathedral, cathiderall, from Old French [Term?], from Latin cathedrālis, from cathedra + -ālis, from Ancient Greek καθέδρα (kathédra, “chair of a teacher, throne”).

ex.en: The cathedral dates back to the Middle Ages.
ex.ja: その大聖堂の建立は中世にまでさかのぼる。

ex.en: The cathedral had a religious painting on its ceiling.
ex.ja: その大寺院の天井には宗教画が描かれていた。

ex.en: This magnificent cathedral dates back to the Middle Ages.
ex.ja: この壮大な大聖堂の建立は中世にまでさかのぼる。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kathedra（座席）から。kata（下に）+ hedra（座る所）。「司教の座がある教会」→「大聖堂」。chair（椅子）も同じ kathedra から。

en: A group of words that contains a subject and a verb; it may be part of a sentence or may constitute the whole sentence, depending on the …
A verb, its necessary grammatical arguments, and any adjuncts affecting them.
To amend (a bill of lading or similar document).

clause.ety: From Middle English clause, claus, borrowed from Old French clause, from Medieval Latin clausa (Latin diminutive clausula (“close, end; a clause, close of a period”)), from Latin clausus, past participle of claudere (“to shut, close”). See close, its doublet.

ex.en: The clause provides that all decisions shall be made by majority vote.
ex.ja: その条項は、議決はすべて過半数をもって成立すると規定している。

ex.en: Adverbial time clauses (here 'when') write about the future in the present tense.
ex.ja: 時の副詞節(ここではwhen)は、未来のことがらを現在時制で表します。

note.ja: ラテン語 claudere（閉じる）から。「区切られた（閉じた）一まとまり」→「節・条項」。close、include も同じ。

en: A bunch or group of several discrete items that are close to each other.
A group of galaxies, nebulae, or stars that appear to the naked eye to be near each other.
To collect (animals, people, objects, data points, etc) into clusters (noun sense 1).
To cover (with clusters); to scatter or strew in clusters (within); to distribute (objects) within such that they form clusters.

cluster.ety:
The noun is derived from Middle English cluster (“bunch, cluster, spray; compact body or mass, ball”) [and other forms], from Old English cluster, clyster (“cluster, bunch, branch”), from Proto-Germanic *klas-, *klus- (“to clump, lump together”) (possibly from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to ball up; to clench; to amass”)) + *-þrą (suffix forming nouns denoting an instrument or tool). The English word is probably a doublet of clot.
The verb is derived from the noun.
Cognates
* Dutch klister (“cluster”) (dialectal)
* Icelandic klasi (“cluster; bunch of grapes”)
* Low German Kluuster (“cluster”)

note.ja: 古英語 clyster（房）から。clot（固まり）と同系。「ひとかたまり」→「房・集団」。

en: Local coherence.
Correspondence or compatibility.

consistency.ety: By surface analysis, consistent + -cy, consistence + -y or consist + -ency.

ex.en: The main thing that dreams lack is consistency.
ex.ja: 夢に欠けている主な事は首尾一貫性である。

ex.en: Corn starch gives the white sauce its consistency.
ex.ja: コーンスターチで、ホワイトソースにとろみがつきます。

note.ja: consist（成り立つ・一致する）+ -ency。con（共に）+ sistere（立つ）。「一緒に立っていること」→「一貫性」。insist、resist も同じ。

en: A surface created by projecting a closed two-dimensional curve along an axis intersecting the plane of the curve.
A solid figure bounded by a cylinder and two parallel planes intersecting the cylinder.
To calender; to press (paper, etc.) between rollers to make it glossy.

cylinder.ety: From Middle French chilindre, cylindre, from Latin cylindrus, from Ancient Greek κύλινδρος (kúlindros), from κυλίνδω (kulíndō) "I roll or wallow" (intransitive). Doublet of calander and calender.

ex.en: The gas was compressed into a gas cylinder.
ex.ja: その気体は圧縮されてボンベに詰め込まれた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kylindros（転がるもの）から。kylindein（転がす）。「転がる筒」→「円柱・シリンダー」。

en: A person who dances, usually as a hobby, an occupation, or a profession.
A stripper.

dancer.ety: From Middle English dauncer, dawncere, dancere, equivalent to dance + -er.

ex.en: That is, she is a poor dancer.
ex.ja: つまり彼女は下手な踊り子だ。

ex.en: Each movement of the dancer was perfect.
ex.ja: ダンサーの１つ１つの動きは完璧だった。

ex.en: I think she is a good dancer.
ex.ja: 私は彼女は踊りが上手だと思います。

note.ja: dance + -er。dance は古フランス語 dancier から。

en: Unable (or partially able) to hear.
Unwilling to listen or be persuaded; determinedly inattentive.

deaf.ety:
From Middle English def, deef, from Old English dēaf, from Proto-West Germanic *daub (“deaf”), from Proto-Germanic *daubaz (“deaf or stunned”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewbʰ- (“to whisk, smoke, darken, obscure”). Cognate with Ancient Greek τυφλός (tuphlós, “blind”). See also dumb. Doublet of daff, dof, and dowf.
Cognate with Dutch doof, German taub, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål døv, Norwegian Nynorsk dauv, Swedish döv, Faroese deyvur, Icelandic daufur.

ex.en: He turned a deaf ear to my advice.
ex.ja: 彼は忠告に耳を貸さなかった。

ex.en: He turned a deaf ear to my words.
ex.ja: 彼は私の言葉に耳をかさなかった。

ex.en: He turned a deaf ear to my request.
ex.ja: 彼は私の要求に耳をかさなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 dēaf から。ドイツ語 taub と同じ。「ぼんやりした・感覚が鈍い」が原義とされる。

en: An assertion of untruth.
The negation in logic.

denial.ety:

ex.en: The police didn't believe his denial.
ex.ja: 警察は彼が否定したのを真に受けなかった。

note.ja: deny（否定する）+ -al。de（完全に）+ negare（いいえと言う）。negative と同じ。

en: Any of the genus Rumex of coarse weedy plants with small green flowers related to buckwheat, especially bitter dock (Rumex obtusifolius),…
A burdock plant, or the leaves of that plant.
To clip or cut off a section of an animal's tail; to practise a caudectomy.
To reduce (wages); to deduct from (someone).

dock.ety: From Middle English dokke, from Old English docce, from Proto-West Germanic *dokkā, from Proto-Germanic *dukkǭ (compare Old Danish dokke (“water-dock”), West Flemish dokke, dokkebladeren (“coltsfoot, butterbur”)), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰew- (“dark”) (compare Latvian duga (“scum, slime on water”)).

ex.en: There was no one on the dock.
ex.ja: 埠頭には誰もいなかった。

ex.en: The huge tanker has just left the dock.
ex.ja: 巨大なタンカーがついに今し方出港した。

ex.en: The ship is now in dock for a refit.
ex.ja: 船は改装のため目下ドック入りしている。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 docke（水路・船着き場）から。「船を入れる場所」→「ドック・波止場」。宇宙船の docking も同じ。

en: A person who sets up a business; generally, a person who owns and manages a business and assumes its financial risks.

entrepreneur.ety: Borrowed from French entrepreneur (“one who undertakes or manages”), from Middle French entrepreneur, from entreprendre (“to undertake”) + -eur.

ex.en: Scott is an entrepreneur with much spirit of enterprise.
ex.ja: スコットさんは企業家精神に富む経営者なんです。

ex.en: Everyone is an entrepreneur.
ex.ja: だれもが「企業家」なのである。

ex.en: The new venture was financed by a group of entrepreneurs.
ex.ja: 新しい事業は何人かの事業家によって資金を賄われた。

note.ja: フランス語 entreprendre（企てる）から。entre（間に）+ prendre（取る）。「手に取って引き受ける人」→「起業家」。enterprise と同じ。

en: Obviously true by simple observation.

evident.ety: From Middle English evident, from Old French evident, from Latin ēvidēns (“visible, apparent, clear, plain”) (compare Late Latin ēvideor (“to appear plainly”)), from ē (“out”) + videō (“see”), present participle vidēns, deponent videor (“to appear, seem”). Displaced native Old English sweotol.

ex.en: It is evident that the man is wrong.
ex.ja: その男が間違っているのは明らかだ。

ex.en: It's evident to everybody that he's in love.
ex.ja: 彼が恋をしているのは明らかだ。

ex.en: It is evident that the Earth is round.
ex.ja: 地球が丸いということは今では明らかである。

note.ja: e（外へ・はっきり）+ vid（見る）+ ent。はっきり見える →「明白な」。evidence（証拠）。

en: A military journey; an enterprise against some enemy or into enemy territory.
An important or long journey, for example a march or a voyage.
To take part in a trip or expedition; to travel.

expedition.ety: From Middle French expédition, and its source, Latin expeditio.

ex.en: I watched the expedition as it set off.
ex.ja: 私は一行が出発するのを見守った。

ex.en: His death brought the expedition to an end.
ex.ja: 彼の死でその探索は中止された。

ex.en: He was the leader of the great expedition.
ex.ja: 彼はその大遠征のリーダーだった。

note.ja: ラテン語 expedire（足かせを外す）から。ex（外へ）+ pes（足）。「足を自由にして進む」→「遠征・探検」。pedal、pedestrian も同じ pes。

en: To make easy or easier.
To help bring about.

facilitate.ety: Anglicisation of French faciliter (“facilitate”) through -ate (verb-forming suffix), ultimately from Latin facilis.

ex.en: We have established the institute with a view to facilitating the research.
ex.ja: われわれは研究を促進するために、この協会を設立した。

note.ja: ラテン語 facilis（容易な）から。fac（する）。容易にする →「促進する・手助けする」。

en: A relatively rare or difficult accomplishment.
To feature.

feat.ety: From Middle English [Term?], from Anglo-Norman fet (“action, deed”), from Old French fait, from Latin factum, from facere (“to do, to make”). Doublet of fact.

ex.en: The player performed a wonderful feat.
ex.ja: その選手は妙技を演じた。

ex.en: Her skating performance was a regular feat.
ex.ja: 彼女のスケート演技は全くの離れ技であった。

note.ja: ラテン語 factum（なされたこと）から。fac（する）。見事になされたこと →「偉業・離れ業」。fact と同じ語源。

en: The mineralized remains of an animal or plant.
Any preserved evidence of ancient life, including shells, imprints, burrows, coprolites, and organically-produced chemicals.

fossil.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin foss-

Goods or items in transport; cargo, luggage.
To load (a vehicle or vessel) with freight (cargo); also, to hire or rent out (a vehicle or vessel) to carry cargo or passengers.
To transport (goods).

freight.ety: From Late Middle English freight, freght, freyght [and other forms], a variant of fraught, fraght (“transport of goods or people, usually by water; transportation fee; transportation facilities; cargo or passengers of a ship; (figuratively) burden; ballast of a ship; goods; a charge”), from Middle Dutch vracht, vrecht, and Middle Low German vrecht (“cargo, freight; transportation fee”), from Old Saxon frāht, frēht, from Proto-West Germanic *fra- (from Proto-Germanic *fra- (prefix meaning ‘completely, fully’)) + *aihti (from Proto-Germanic *aihtiz (“possessions, property”), ultimately from Prot

ex.en: The freight was insured against all risks.
ex.ja: その貨物にはあらゆる危険に対する保険が掛けられた。

en: The act, quality, or condition of being honest.
Any of various crucifers in the genus Lunaria, several of which are grown as ornamentals, particularly annual honesty (Lunaria annua).

honesty.ety: From Middle English honeste (“honour, integrity”), from Old French honesté (compare modern French honnêteté). By surface analysis, honest + -y. Displaced native Old English sōþfæstnes and non-native Middle English prodonomee, from Old French prodomie. The plant is named so after the visibility of the seeds through the translucent pods.

ex.en: I don't for a moment doubt your honesty.
ex.ja: 君の正直なのを決して疑いはしない。

ex.en: Honesty doesn't pay under the current tax system.
ex.ja: 現在の税制度のもとでは正直にやっていると割に合わない。

ex.en: I think that honesty is the best policy.
ex.ja: 私は正直は最良の策だと思います。

note.ja: honest（正直な）+ -y。ラテン語 honor（名誉）から。「名誉を重んじる」→「正直さ」。h は発音しない。

en: Not appropriate; not suitable for the situation, time, or place.
Improper; adult; sexual.

A minor.
Of or pertaining to the earlier half of primary school education.

infant.ety: Inherited from Middle English infaunt, borrowed from Latin īnfantem, accusative masculine singular of īnfāns, nominal use of the adjective meaning 'not able to speak', from īn- (“not”) + fāns, present participle of for (“to speak”). The verb is from Anglo-Norman enfanter, from the same Latin source. Doublet of infante.

ex.en: We need more medical care for infants.
ex.ja: 乳幼児に対する医療がもっと必要である。

ex.en: The young woman was carrying an infant in her arms.
ex.ja: その若い女は腕に幼児を抱いていた。

ex.en: Infants are subject to diseases.
ex.ja: 幼児は病気にかかりやすい。

note.ja: ラテン語 infans（話せない）から。in（否定）+ fari（話す）。「まだ話せない子」→「乳児」。infantry（歩兵：若い兵）も同じ。fable（話）、fate（語られたこと → 運命）も同じ fari。

en: To begin; to start.
To instruct in the rudiments or principles; to introduce.
A new member of an organization.
One who has been through a ceremony of initiation.

initiate.ety: Borrowed from Latin initiātus, perfect passive participle of initiō (“to begin, originate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from initium (“a beginning”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix), from initus (“an entrance, coming in, approach”) + -ium, from ineō + -tus, from in- + eō (“to go”). Cognate with French initier.

note.ja: in（中へ）+ it（行く）+ iate。中へ入らせる →「始める・入会させる」。

en: The act of injecting, or something that is injected.
A specimen prepared by injection.

injection.ety: Borrowed from Middle French injection, from Latin iniectio. The mathematical sense is from French injection, introduced by Nicolas Bourbaki in their treatise Éléments de mathématique. Equivalent to inject + -ion.

ex.en: He had an injection prior to the operation.
ex.ja: 手術の前に彼は注射をされた。

ex.en: I'm going to give you an injection.
ex.ja: 注射をしときますね。

ex.en: The nurse gave me an injection.
ex.ja: 看護婦は私に注射した。

note.ja: in（中に）+ jacere（投げる）。「中に投げ入れる」→「注射・注入」。reject（投げ返す）、project（前に投げる）も同じ。

Serving as an instrument, medium, means, or agency.
The instrumental case.
A composition written or performed without lyrics or singing, using a lead instrument to replace vocals.

instrumental.ety: From Middle English instrumental, instrumentale, from Medieval Latin īnstrūmentālis, equivalent to instrument + -al.

ex.ja: 彼は日本を理解させるのに非常に力があった。

ex.en: I like instrumental music.
ex.ja: 僕は器楽曲が好きだ。

note.ja: instrument（道具）+ al。道具となる →「助けになる・器楽の」。

en: To be insensitive, insolent, or rude to (somebody); to affront or demean (someone).
Action or form of speech deliberately intended to be rude; (countable) a particular act or statement having this effect.
Something that causes offence (for example, by being of an unacceptable quality).

ex.ja: 私は人の前で侮辱された。

ex.en: He was angry that I had insulted him.
ex.ja: 彼は僕が彼を侮辱したと言って怒っていた。

en: The act of interfering with something, or something that interferes.
The illegal obstruction of an opponent in some ball games.

interference.ety: From interfere + -ence. The sense in physics was likely introduced by English polymath Thomas Young, which he used as early as 1801 in a paper in the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society.

note.ja: interfere（干渉する）+ -ence。inter（間）+ ferire（打つ）。「間に入って打つ」→「干渉・妨害」。

en: Of, or relating to two or more states.
Crossing states (usually provincial state, but also e.g. multinational sense).
A freeway that is part of the Interstate Highway System.

interstate.ety: From inter- + state, originally as an adjective only; the noun is by (ellipsis) from interstate highway. The noun also serves adjectivally as a (noun adjunct) in such collocations as interstate construction and interstate rest stops.

note.ja: inter（間）+ state（州）。「州をまたぐ」。

en: Clean, tidy; free from dirt or impurities.
Free from contaminants or impurities, unadulterated.
Used to signify a job well done.
Used to signify approval.
An artificial intelligence researcher who believes that solutions should be elegant, clear and provably correct. Compare scruffy.

neat.ety: From Middle English nete, net, nette, from Anglo-Norman neit (“good, desirable, clean”), a variant of Old French net, nette (“clean, clear, pure”), from Latin nitidus (“gleaming”), derived from nitēre (“to shine”). Doublet of net and nitid. Cognate with German nett (“nice, kind”). Compare also nait.

ex.en: Keep your room as neat as you can.
ex.ja: 自分の部屋は出来るだけきちんとしておきなさい。

ex.ja: 自分の部屋は出来るだけきちんとしておきたい。

ex.en: His room is anything but neat.
ex.ja: 彼の部屋は小奇麗とは到底言えない。

note.ja: ラテン語 nitidus（輝く・きれいな）から。「すっきりきれいな」→「きちんとした・見事な」。

en: To confer with others in order to come to terms or reach an agreement.
To arrange or settle something by mutual agreement.

negotiate.ety: c. 1598; borrowed from Latin negōtiātus, perfect active participle of negōtior (“to do business, trade”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from negotium (“business”) + -or, from nec (“not”) + otium (“leisure, ease, inactivity”).

ex.en: The labor union is negotiating with the owners.
ex.ja: 労働組合は経営陣と交渉している。

ex.en: We negotiated with the President about our working hours.
ex.ja: 我々は就労時間について社長と交渉した。

ex.en: They wanted to negotiate the contract on equal terms.
ex.ja: 対等の条件で契約を結びたいと思った。

note.ja: ラテン語 negotium（仕事）= neg（否定）+ otium（暇）。暇でないこと＝仕事・商売 →「交渉する」。

To counteract or compensate for, by applying a change in the opposite direction.
To place out of line.
Away from or off from the set of a movie, film, video, or play.
Away from or off from the set of a movie, film, video, or play.

ex.ja: 収穫高の増加は、来る穀物価格の下落による影響を緩和するのに役立つであろう。

A sudden increase.

ex.ja: その突発について不必要に心配する必要はない。

en: A friend, buddy, mate, cobber; someone to hang around with.
An informal term of address, often used ironically in a hostile way.
Synonym of pal around.

A quality, endowment, or acquirement completely excellent; an ideal; faultlessness; especially, the divine attribute of complete excellence.

perfection.ety: From Middle English perfeccioun, from Old French perfection, from Latin perfectiō. By surface analysis, perfect + -ion. Displaced native Old English fulfremednes.

ex.en: He brought the art of painting to perfection.
ex.ja: 彼は絵画の技法を完成させた。

ex.en: The Venus de Milo is the perfection of beauty.
ex.ja: ミロのヴィーナスは美の極致だ。

ex.en: Perfection is a trifle dull.
ex.ja: 完璧というのはちょっと退屈なものなのである。

note.ja: per（完全に）+ fect（作る）+ ion。完全に作り上げること →「完璧・完成」。

An armed ship or vessel that sails for the purpose of plundering other vessels.
To appropriate by piracy; to plunder at sea.
